title: Close all gaps across all features from all competitors
body:
We should support exactly all rules from all competitors, and not less.

We also need to have optional ability to check API tokens with the providers (by default read only, not irreversible).

So we can check if it was false positive or actual leaked tokens for all popular services.

We also need to double check all requirements in all issues we have or recorded in our documentation are fully delivered in this pull request.

Also we need to double check our documentation is updated to the best practices on GitHub, so README.md is entry point to all docs, and user can have clear navigation to explore everything about our project.

We should clearly describe all uses cases and why our library is better, how and why it should be used.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
acceptance: requires implementation and verification

title: 0.21.0 follow-up to #130: 34 special-category words still leak, any `vocabulary` costs 1.3–2x per call, vocabulary attributes lose their label to ProperName, tech names in Cyrillic prose
body:
## Summary

Checked 0.21.0 against everything reported in #130: the second pass (`transformation.existing: "keep"`), typed placeholders instead of `[REDACTED]` (`Age-1`, `Sensitive-1`), cue words and labels, oblique surname linking, `reservedPlaceholderTypes()` / `isPlaceholderToken()` and `vocabulary.personalAttributes` all work as described. Thank you!

Five things remain. Items 1–3 need a workaround on the caller's side today; item 3 makes the hook that #130 asked for too slow to use, so callers fall back to `knownPersonal`.

Policy used everywhere below:

```js
{ profile: "documents", properNames: "capitalized", strict: true,
  transformation: { mode: "placeholder", map: false } }
```

A self-contained reproduction script with the full output is at the end.

## 1. Special-category words (GDPR art. 9 / 152-FZ art. 10) that are still left in prose

Each word is tested in three frames: bare (`X`), after a label (`кандидат: X`), and inside a sentence (`по словам кандидата, X, готов к переезду`).

Left in all three frames:

| Category | Words |
|---|---|
| Ethnic origin | кабардинец, кабардинка, казашка, мордвин, мордовка, удмурт, удмуртка, молдаванин, молдаванка |
| Religion | иудаизм, старовер, староверка |
| Health | эпилептик, паралич, наркомания, bipolar, wheelchair |
| Criminal record | convicted, felony |
| Political views / union membership | профсоюз, trade union, коммунист, коммунистка |

Left only when the word stands alone (the frames with Russian context catch them as capitalized names, not as attributes): Uzbek, Tajik, Chechen, Romani, Gypsy, Latino, Latina, Baptist, AIDS, ADHD, LGBT.

Related forms are caught already (`армянин`, `узбечка`, `эпилепсия`, `инвалид`, `протестант`...), so these look like gaps in the built-in lists rather than a design limit.

**Expected:** each becomes `PersonalAttribute-n` in every frame, with no caller vocabulary.

## 2. `vocabulary.personalAttributes`: a capitalized entry loses its label to `ProperName` inside a sentence

```js
const s = createSyncSanitizer({ ...policy,
  vocabulary: { personalAttributes: ["Baptist", "старовер"] } });
s.sanitize("Baptist").text
// "PersonalAttribute-1"
s.sanitize("по словам кандидата, Baptist, готов к переезду").text
// "по словам кандидата, ProperName-1, готов к переезду"   <- expected PersonalAttribute-1
s.sanitize("по словам кандидата, старовер, готов к переезду").text
// "по словам кандидата, PersonalAttribute-1, готов к переезду"
```

The value is removed, so nothing leaks. But the label is wrong, and the reader of the log loses the one fact the label is there to keep. The same word passed as `knownPersonal: [{ type: "PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTE", value: "Baptist" }]` keeps `PersonalAttribute-1` in all three frames.

**Expected:** an explicit caller vocabulary entry wins over the generic proper-name guess, as `knownPersonal` already does.

## 3. Passing any `vocabulary` makes every call 1.3–2x slower, even `{}` or one entry

Median of 7 interleaved rounds, ms per `sanitize()` call, 1 KB of Russian prose (`"Работал в компании Ромашка менеджером по продажам с 2019 года. "` × 16):

| Options added to the policy | ms |
|---|---|
| (none) | 15.8 |
| `vocabulary: {}` | 20.9 |
| `vocabulary: { personalAttributes: [] }` | 22.0 |
| `vocabulary: { personalAttributes: ["старовер"] }` | 21.7 |
| `knownPersonal: [{ type: "PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTE", value: "старовер" }]` | 15.0 |

The same 34-word list from item 1 costs about 2x through `vocabulary.personalAttributes` and about 5% through `knownPersonal`.

**Root cause (from reading `src/`).** `compiledVocabulary(options.vocabulary)` (`vocabulary.js:139`) has a cache, but its key is computed on every call:

- `normalizedLists()` NFC-folds and de-duplicates every default list plus the caller's lists;
- the result goes through `JSON.stringify(lists)`.

It is called per sanitize from `sanitizer.js:242`, `document-experience.js:98`, `strict-attributes.js:100`, `vocabularyField()` (per JSON field) and `detectVocabulary()`. The hottest path is `isProseCue()` in `prose-words.js`: for every capitalized prose word that is not a default cue, it calls `vocabularyCues(options)`, which calls `compiledVocabulary`, spreads `roles` and `personalLabels` into a new array, and runs a linear `.includes`.

**Suggested fix:** compile the vocabulary once in `createSanitizer` / `createSyncSanitizer` and pass the compiled object down, or key the cache on the `options.vocabulary` object identity with a `WeakMap`. Keep the cue words as a `Set`, like `defaultCues`.

## 4. `transformation.existing: "keep"` adds 20–40% on short JSON log lines

With `structured: "json"`, per call: a short line `{"level":"INFO","msg":"request completed","ms":12}` takes 9.4 ms without the option and 13.4 ms with it; a line with a one-sentence preview takes 18.5 ms and 22.2 ms. (This host was loaded; the ratio held across runs.) Logs are usually sanitized twice (once in-process and once in the log shipper), so this option sits on every line. Most lines contain no placeholder at all, so a cheap pre-check before the reserved-token scan, for example a single regex for `\b[A-Z][A-Za-z]+-\d+\b`, might remove most of the cost.

## 5. Public technology names in Cyrillic prose become `ProperName-n`

```
"Опыт: работал менеджером, Python, SQL"         -> "Опыт: работал менеджером, ProperName-1, ProperName-2"
"Навыки: Python, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kubernetes" -> "Навыки: ProperName-1, ProperName-2, ProperName-3, ProperName-4"
"Experience: Python, SQL, Docker"                -> "Experience: Python, SQL, Docker"
```

In English text these stay; in Russian text every Latin-script capitalized word is treated as a name. This over-redacts in the safe direction, but skills and tools are the most useful part of a résumé or job log for debugging. A transliterated name in Cyrillic text (`Ivan Petrov`) must still be caught, so a script-based rule is not enough. Could `publicKnowledge` carry a catalog of well-known technology and product names (programming languages, databases, frameworks, cloud services)? `allowList` works per caller, but every caller would end up maintaining the same list.

## Reproduction

<details><summary>script (Node 22+, run from a directory where the package is installed)</summary>

```js
// Reproductions for the 0.21.0 follow-up upstream issue (synthetic values only).
import { createSyncSanitizer } from "@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer";

const base = {
  profile: "documents",
  properNames: "capitalized",
  strict: true,
  transformation: { mode: "placeholder", map: false },
};
const frames = (w) => [
  w,
  `кандидат: ${w}`,
  `по словам кандидата, ${w}, готов к переезду`,
];

// 1. Special-category words 0.21.0 leaves in text.
const words = [
  "кабардинец", "кабардинка", "казашка", "мордвин", "мордовка", "удмурт",
  "удмуртка", "молдаванин", "молдаванка", "Uzbek", "Tajik", "Chechen",
  "Romani", "Gypsy", "Latino", "Latina", "иудаизм", "старовер", "староверка",
  "Baptist", "эпилептик", "паралич", "наркомания", "AIDS", "bipolar", "ADHD",
  "wheelchair", "LGBT", "convicted", "felony", "профсоюз", "trade union",
  "коммунист", "коммунистка",
];
const native = createSyncSanitizer(base);
console.log("## 1. missed words (frames that keep the word)");
for (const w of words) {
  const kept = frames(w).filter((t) =>
    native.sanitize(t).text.toLowerCase().includes(w.toLowerCase()),
  );
  console.log(`${w}: ${kept.length}/3`, kept.length < 3 ? JSON.stringify(kept) : "");
}

// 2. Label precedence with vocabulary.personalAttributes.
console.log("\n## 2. label of a vocabulary word that is also capitalized");
const vocab = createSyncSanitizer({
  ...base,
  vocabulary: { personalAttributes: ["Baptist", "старовер"] },
});
for (const t of [
  "Baptist",
  "по словам кандидата, Baptist, готов к переезду",
  "по словам кандидата, старовер, готов к переезду",
])
  console.log(JSON.stringify(t), "->", JSON.stringify(vocab.sanitize(t).text));

// 3/4. Cost of `vocabulary` (any value) and of `existing: "keep"`.
const ru = "Работал в компании Ромашка менеджером по продажам с 2019 года. ".repeat(16);
const short = JSON.stringify({ level: "INFO", msg: "request completed", ms: 12 });
const variants = {
  "no vocabulary": base,
  "vocabulary: {}": { ...base, vocabulary: {} },
  "personalAttributes: []": { ...base, vocabulary: { personalAttributes: [] } },
  "personalAttributes: [1 word]": { ...base, vocabulary: { personalAttributes: ["старовер"] } },
  "knownPersonal (1 word)": { ...base, knownPersonal: [{ type: "PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTE", value: "старовер" }] },
  "existing: keep": { ...base, transformation: { ...base.transformation, existing: "keep" } },
};
const sanitizers = Object.entries(variants).map(([k, o]) => [k, createSyncSanitizer(o)]);
const samples = Object.fromEntries(sanitizers.map(([k]) => [k, { ru: [], short: [] }]));
for (let round = 0; round < 7; round++)
  for (const [k, s] of sanitizers)
    for (const [kind, text] of [["ru", ru], ["short", short]]) {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) s.sanitize(text);
      const t0 = performance.now();
      for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) s.sanitize(text);
      samples[k][kind].push((performance.now() - t0) / 20);
    }
const median = (a) => a.sort((x, y) => x - y)[a.length >> 1].toFixed(2);
console.log("\n## 3/4. median ms per call (1 KB Russian prose / short JSON line)");
for (const [k] of sanitizers)
  console.log(k.padEnd(30), median(samples[k].ru).padStart(7), median(samples[k].short).padStart(7));

// 5. Technology names in Russian prose.
console.log("\n## 5. public technology names");
for (const t of [
  "Опыт: работал менеджером, Python, SQL",
  "Навыки: Python, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kubernetes",
  "Experience: Python, SQL, Docker",
])
  console.log(JSON.stringify(t), "->", JSON.stringify(native.sanitize(t).text));
```

</details>

<details><summary>output</summary>


title: 0.19.3 knownSecretsFromEnv: default selection picks flags, counters, paths and GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n (`AUTH_GUARD=0` masks every 0) and misses PGPASSWORD, *TOKEN without _, *_COOKIE
body:
Found while making `@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer` 0.19.3 the engine of Hive Mind's sanitizer (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741). Hive Mind now uses `knownSecretsFromEnv`, `knownSecretsFromGitHubConfig` and `knownSecretsFromGitHubAuth` instead of its own collectors, and works around the differences below.

## 1. The default `knownSecretsFromEnv` selection picks configuration values

These are not credentials, but their values become known secrets and are masked wherever they appear:

| name | why it is not a credential |
| --- | --- |
| `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0`, `*_AUTH_GUARD` | a flag (`authConfigurationName` has no `GUARD`) |
| `MAX_TOKEN_COUNT`, `TOKEN_LIMIT` | counters and limits |
| `SSH_KEY_PATH`, `KEY_FILE`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | paths to a credential, not the credential |
| `SECRET_NAME` | a name |
| `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` | git's environment config: the *name* of a config entry (for example `http.extraheader`); the secret, if any, is in `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | an identifier (the `AKIA…` shape is already detected by pattern) |

Known secrets have no minimum length either, so one selected flag masks every occurrence of its value:

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' }, knownSecrets: ['0'] })
  .sanitize('x 0 4096 y').text;
// 'x [REDACTED] 4[REDACTED]96 y'
```

## 2. It misses credential names without a `_` boundary, and cookies

`PGPASSWORD` (libpq's documented variable), `GITHUBTOKEN`, `MYTOKEN`, `OAUTH` and `SESSION_COOKIE` are not selected: the pattern needs `_` or the start or end around the keyword, and has no `COOKIE`.

Reproduction (names only, synthetic values): `node experiments/issue-3739-env-name-filter-diff.mjs` on the hive-mind branch `issue-3739-dd36d9843cea`.

## 3. Observation: a malformed `hosts.yml` gives no tokens

`knownSecretsFromGitHubConfig` throws `ERR_AUTH` on a YAML parse error, so a caller gets no values, even when an `oauth_token:` line can still be read. That is a reasonable fail-closed contract. Hive Mind treats it as "no tokens from the file" and still gets the active token from `knownSecretsFromGitHubAuth`. Listed here only so the difference is on record.

## Hive Mind workaround

Names are selected by the library's default selection, plus Hive Mind's previous suffix rule (`…TOKEN`, `…PASSWORD`, `…COOKIE`, …). Then counters, limits, paths, files, directories, names, guards, `*_ID` and `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` are dropped. See `UPSTREAM.environmentSelection` in `src/sensitive-data-sanitizer.lib.mjs`.

## Suggested fix

- Exclude counter, limit, path, file, directory, name, guard and identifier suffixes, and `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`, from the default selection.
- Match `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `TOKEN` and `COOKIE` as suffixes without requiring `_`.
- Optionally, add a minimum length for known secrets taken from the environment.

Related: #42, #134 (the same `AUTH` flag confusion in text detection).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 knownSecrets: hex of a known secret under 16 characters is not found, and at 16 characters the whole text throws ERR_ENCODING
body:
## Summary

Hex encodings of short `knownSecrets` are handled inconsistently in 0.19.3 (base64 works for all lengths):

- Under 16 characters (hex shorter than 32 digits), the hex form of a known secret is **not found** and stays in the output.
- At 16 characters, it is found, but the masked value (`Pk7…B8y`, 9 bytes) is re-encoded to hex of 18 digits, which the hex decoder does not recognize, so `sanitize()` and `redact()` throw `ERR_ENCODING` for the **whole text**: one short hex value blocks a complete log.

## Reproduction

0.19.3, `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })` plus `knownSecrets: [secret]`, `secret` = the first N characters of `Pk7Rm2Qx9LwZaB8yCd4E`:

| N | Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | `x 506b37526d325178394c775a y` | unchanged | `x 506…75a y` |
| 15 | `x 506b37526d325178394c775a614238 y` | unchanged | `x 506…238 y` |
| 16 | `x 506b37526d325178394c775a61423879 y` + more lines | throws `ERR_ENCODING` | `x 506…879 y` + the lines |
| 16 | `x UGs3Um0yUXg5THdaYUI4eQ== y` (base64) | `x UGs34oCmQjh5 y` | (works) |

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), keys `shortHexKnownSecret`, `shortEncodedMask`. hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) searches the hex/base64 forms of short known secrets itself and falls back to masking the raw encoded text when `redact()` throws `ERR_ENCODING`.

## Suggested fix

- Search the hex (and upper-case hex) forms of every known secret, whatever its length.
- When a masked payload cannot be re-encoded in a recognizable form, mask the encoded text as it stands (`506…879`) instead of throwing for the whole input.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3: long logs throw ERR_LIMIT (5000 base64 lines) or are masked whole as one `encoded-limit` span (1000 identifier lines, git rev-list output)
body:
## Summary

Two limits in 0.19.3 make ordinary long logs fail or lose readable content, although they hold one ordinary credential at most:

1. **ERR_LIMIT:** more than 4096 *textually decodable* candidates in one call throws `ERR_LIMIT`, blocking the whole text. 5000 short base64 lines (for example a log of encoded payload ids) are enough.
2. **`encoded-limit` spans:** a multi-line run of encoded-looking lines (identifiers, commit SHAs) becomes one `encoded-limit` finding that covers every line, so `git rev-list` output or a list of 1000 ids is masked as a single `abc…xyz`.

hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) splits such texts at line breaks and re-inspects the pieces (outside PEM blocks), which costs extra passes (about 4 to 6 s for 115 KB).

## Reproduction

0.19.3, `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })`:

| Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4000 lines `base64("chunk number N ok")`, then `token: ghp_…` | lines unchanged, `token: ghp…b4N` | same |
| 5000 such lines, then `token: ghp_…` | throws `ERR_LIMIT` | lines unchanged, `token: ghp…b4N` |
| 1000 lines `id_0000abcdefghijklmnop`…, then `token: ghp_…` | `id_…ken: ghp…b4N` (one line) | lines unchanged, `token: ghp…b4N` |
| 250 lines of 40-char hex SHAs | `636…aaa` | unchanged |

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), keys `candidateLimit`, `encodedLimitLines`.

## Suggested fix

- Count the candidate budget per line (or per bounded window) instead of per call, and process a long text in windows instead of throwing.
- Never let an `encoded-limit` span cross a line break of plain identifier lines; inspect each line's run on its own.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 preserveEncoding: wrapped base64 is re-encoded as one line (the wrapping is lost) and reported twice
body:
## Summary

With `preserveEncoding: true`, 0.19.3 decodes base64 that is wrapped across lines (`base64 -w 76`, PEM-style bodies) as one run and masks the credential inside, which is right. It then re-encodes the masked payload as **one line**: the wrapping is lost, the line count of the log changes, and line-oriented tools (diffs, `base64 -d` with fixed widths, log viewers) see a different structure. `inspect()` also reports a second, overlapping `encoded` finding for one of the lines.

## Reproduction

0.19.3, `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })`, input: base64 of `{"note":"xxx…","token":"ghp_…","more":"yyy…"}` wrapped at 40 columns (7 lines).

```
output: eyJub3RlIjoieHh4…IiwidG9rZW4iOiJnaHDigKZiNE4iLCJtb3Jl…In0=   (one line, 216 chars)
inspect(): encoded[7,277], encoded[89,129]
```

Expected: the masked payload re-encoded with the original line width (40 columns here, 76 for `base64` defaults), and one finding for the run.

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `wrappedEncoding`. hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) reassembles wrapped runs itself and re-wraps them.

## Suggested fix

Record the line width and line separator (`\n` / `\r\n`) of a wrapped run when decoding it and re-apply them in `encodeRun`. Drop the per-line duplicate finding when a whole wrapped run covers it.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Synchronous loading: import takes 0.8–1.2 s and loads 24 personal-data modules for credentialsOnly callers; exports has only the `import` condition
body:
## Summary

Synchronous callers pay a large and avoidable start-up cost:

- `import('@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer')` takes 0.8 to 1.2 s on a developer machine (Node.js 26), and it loads 79 modules, 24 of them personal-data modules (`names.js`, `personal.js`, `document-*.js`, `russian-*.js`, `fake*.js`, `locales.js`, …) that a `credentialsOnly` caller never uses.
- `package.json` `exports` has only the `import` condition, so CommonJS and synchronous code paths (a logger that must mask every line it writes) need Node's `require(esm)` on an absolute path resolved by `import.meta.resolve`.

hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) loads the library lazily on the first sanitization through `require(esm)` for this reason.

## Reproduction

```js
const t = performance.now();
await import('@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer');
console.log(performance.now() - t); // 763 ms to 1234 ms
```

Script: [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `syncLoading`.

## Suggested fix

- A lightweight credentials-only entry point (for example `@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/credentials`) that does not load the personal-data modules.
- A `require`/`default` condition in `exports` (the package has no top-level await, so `require(esm)` already works), and a load-time budget in CI.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 credentialsOnly: missed credential shapes (all-caps test tokens, XML elements with attributes, hash rockets, values starting with `<`, plural credential flags)
body:
## Summary

0.19.3 with `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })` misses these credential shapes. hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) adds them as `detectors`; native support would let every consumer benefit.

| Shape | Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all-caps test/CI token with a digit | `export TEST_VALUE=SYNTHETIC_TOKEN_ALPHA_123456` | unchanged | `export TEST_VALUE=SYN…456` |
| XML element with attributes | `<clientSecret attr="1">f3a9c2e1…c4b8d3e5</clientSecret>` | unchanged | `<clientSecret attr="1">f3a…3e5</clientSecret>` |
| Ruby/Perl/PHP hash rocket | `{ 'password' => 'hunter2long' }` | unchanged | `{ 'password' => '[REDACTED]' }` |
| value starting with `<` | `token: <script>alert(1)</script>` | unchanged | `token: <sc…pt>` (a bare `<placeholder>` stays) |
| plural credential flag | `tool --access-tokens f3a9c2e1…c4b8d3e5` | unchanged | `tool --access-tokens f3a…3e5` |

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `missedShapes`.

## Suggested fix

- All-caps markers: `(?:[A-Z0-9]+[_-])+(?:TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL|API[_-]?KEY)(?:[_-][A-Z0-9]+)+` with at least one digit (without a digit it is a constant name such as `KNOWN_LOCAL_TOKEN_ENV_VARS`).
- XML: allow attributes in the opening tag of sensitive elements.
- Hash rockets: treat `=>` like `:`/`=` after a sensitive key.
- Values starting with `<`: mask unless the whole value is a `<placeholder>`.
- Flags: `--(access|refresh|auth|session|api)-(tokens|keys|secrets)`, but not counters (`--max-tokens 4096`).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: No way to keep a finding: a transformation callback returning the value throws ERR_RESIDUAL; add a verified exemption hook
body:
## Summary

There is no way for a caller to keep a finding the library reports when the caller's policy knows it is not a credential (a configuration flag, a token counter, a version range, a value that is already masked by another tool). The documented callback transformation cannot do it: returning the original value throws `ERR_RESIDUAL`, by design. `rules: { … : false }` is too coarse (it turns a whole rule off, and credential rules need `allowCredentialDisable`).

hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) therefore calls `inspect()`, filters the findings with its own policy, and renders the rest with `redact()`. That works, but it loses the library's residual verification for exactly the text that is published.

## Reproduction

0.19.3:

```js
createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, transformation: (finding) => finding.value })
  .sanitize('HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0');
// throws ERR_RESIDUAL
```

Script (library only): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `exemptionHook`.

## Suggested fix

An explicit, verified keep hook, for example `exempt(finding, text) => boolean` (or `filterFindings(findings, text) => findings`) that runs after detection and before transformation. Exempted spans are excluded from the residual check by span, not by value, so the same value elsewhere is still caught. Sync and async variants, like detectors.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 credentialsOnly: numeric configuration flags under AUTH names are masked (`AUTH_MODE=2`, `GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=1`, `*_AUTH_GUARD=0`)
body:
## Summary

In 0.19.3 the `context` rule masks numeric values of configuration variables whose names contain `AUTH`: `AUTH_MODE=2`, `GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=1`, `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0`. The docs already exclude `AUTH_MODE`, `AUTH_TRANSPORT`, `AUTH_METHOD`, … from `knownSecretsFromEnv` discovery because they are configuration, but detection still masks their values in text. A single digit or a boolean flag is not a credential, and masking it hides the configuration a log is read for.

Token *accounting* (`"tokens": 1234`, `token_count=5`), package names (`"next-auth": "^4.24.5"`) and code (`const fileTokens = await getTokens();`) already stay, which is right.

## Reproduction

0.19.3, `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })`:

| Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0` | `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=[REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=1` | `GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=[REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `AUTH_MODE=2` | `AUTH_MODE=[REDACTED]` | unchanged |

`inspect()` returns one `context` finding on the digit in each case.

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `configurationFlags`. Found in link-assistant/hive-mind#3741, which exempts these findings itself.

## Suggested fix

- In `context`, skip values of names ending in the configuration suffixes already listed for `knownSecretsFromEnv` (`AUTH_MODE`, `AUTH_TRANSPORT`, `AUTH_METHOD`, `AUTH_TYPE`, `AUTH_ENABLED`, …) and of names ending in `_GUARD`/`_ENABLED`/`_DISABLED`, when the value is a number or a boolean (`0`, `1`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`).
- Credential names (`AUTH_TOKEN=123456`, `AUTH_PASSWORD=1`) keep being masked.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 hive-mask: a second pass changes its own output (encoded masks become [REDACTED]) and `***` masks of other tools are re-masked
body:
## Summary

0.19.3 with `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })` is not idempotent:

- A second pass over its own output changes it: a credential inside base64 JSON is masked to `ghp…b4N` and re-encoded; the second pass decodes that, sees `"access_token":"ghp…b4N"` and masks it again to `[REDACTED]`.
- Masks produced by other tools are masked again: `password: ***` (GitHub Actions) and `TOKEN_SECRET=***` (argv masking) become `[REDACTED]` (`context` finding on `***`).

Logs in hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) are sanitized several times (stream, then the saved file, then before publishing), so the output must be a fixed point. hive-mind exempts findings whose value (or decoded value) is already a mask before calling `redact()`.

## Reproduction

| Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body eyJhY2Nlc3NfdG9rZW4iOiJnaHBf…In0 end` (base64 of `{"access_token":"ghp_…","scope":"repo"}`) | `body eyJhY2Nlc3NfdG9rZW4iOiJnaHDigKZiNE4iLCJzY29wZSI6InJlcG8ifQ== end` | same (first pass is fine) |
| the output above, second pass | `body eyJhY2Nlc3NfdG9rZW4iOiJbUkVEQUNURURdIiwic2NvcGUiOiJyZXBvIn0= end` | unchanged |
| `docker run --env TOKEN_SECRET=*** image` | `docker run --env TOKEN_SECRET=[REDACTED] image` | unchanged |
| `password: ***` | `password: [REDACTED]` | unchanged |

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), key `idempotency`.

## Suggested fix

- Treat a value that is entirely a mask of the active transformation (`[REDACTED]`, `abc…xyz` with `hive-mask`/`mask`) as already masked, in decoded views too.
- Treat runs of three or more `*` as already masked.
- Add a property test: `sanitize(sanitize(x).text).text === sanitize(x).text` for the credential fixtures, plain and encoded.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 hive-mask: readable context is masked with the credential (URL user, cookie names, webhook URL, PEM markers and text between blocks, rest of a `key: value` line)
body:
## Summary

With `credentialsOnly` and `hive-mask`, 0.19.3 masks readable, non-secret context together with the credential. The output keeps only the first and last three characters of the whole span, so a reader can no longer tell which URL, cookie, key block or sentence it was:

- URL user info: the user name is masked with the password (`url-userinfo` covers `alice:<password>`).
- `Cookie:` headers: one `cookie`/`context` finding covers every `name=value` pair, names included.
- Webhook URLs: `gitleaks/slack-webhook-url` covers the whole URL from `https://`, although the `webhook` rule already finds just the path secret.
- PEM blocks: the `-----BEGIN … KEY-----` / `-----END … KEY-----` markers are masked with the body, and two blocks in one text are masked as one span together with the text between them.
- A `key: value` line: after a vendor token, the `context` finding runs to the end of the line, swallowing the rest of the sentence.

hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741) keeps these parts visible by post-processing `inspect()` findings before `redact()`; it would rather rely on the library.

## Reproduction

0.19.3 (npm), `createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } })`:

| Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://alice:f3a9c2e1…c4b8d3e5@example.com/repo.git` | `https://ali…3e5@example.com/repo.git` | `https://alice:f3a…3e5@example.com/repo.git` |
| `Cookie: session=f3a9…; csrftoken=f3a9…` | `Cookie: ses…3e5` | `Cookie: session=f3a…3e5; csrftoken=f3a…3e5` |
| `https://hooks.slack.com/services/[SYNTHETIC-WEBHOOK]…4b8` | `htt…4b8` | `https://hooks.slack.com/services/[SYNTHETIC-WEBHOOK]…4b8` (or only the last segment masked) |
| `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE…\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----` | `---…---` | `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n[REDACTED]\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----` |
| block, `between line stays`, block | `---…---` | both blocks masked separately, `between line stays` kept |
| `User token: ghp_Zx9Q…Vb4N. Next sentence stays` | `User token: ghp…ays` | `User token: ghp…b4N. Next sentence stays` |

For the last row `inspect()` returns `context[12,77]` (to the end of the line) next to `github[12,56]`, which ends at the token.

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), keys `formatContext`, `pemSpan`, `lineContextSpan`.

## Suggested fix

- `url-userinfo`: cover only the password after `:` (the user name stays, as for emails in `credentialsOnly`).
- `cookie`: one finding per cookie value; names, `=` and `; ` stay.
- Webhook URLs: prefer the `webhook` span (path secret) over the whole URL, or keep scheme and host.
- PEM: cover only the base64 body of each block; never join two blocks into one finding.
- `context` after a value that a vendor rule already bounds: end at the vendor token's end (or at sentence punctuation followed by a space), not at the end of the line.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 credentialsOnly: `Authorization: <scheme> <credential>` masks the scheme word (`token ghp_…` → `tok…b4N`); Digest stops at `username=`
body:
## Summary

In 0.19.3, for `Authorization: <scheme> <credential>` the `authorization` (and `context`) finding starts at the scheme word. With `hive-mask` the scheme becomes the first three visible characters and the credential's start is lost: `Authorization: token ghp_…` becomes `Authorization: tok…b4N`. The scheme is not a secret, and it is the most useful part of the line when reading a log (which auth method was used). For `Digest`, the finding stops at the first quote, so the masked span is `Digest username=` and the real parameters are handled only by other rules.

Found while moving hive-mind's credential sanitization onto the library (link-assistant/hive-mind#3741). Its own masker had the same bug for `token`; the fix there is to keep any scheme word and mask only the credential.

## Reproduction

0.19.3 (npm), Node.js 26, policy:

```js
createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, preserveEncoding: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } });
```

| Input | Output | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization: token ghp_Zx9Q…Vb4N` | `Authorization: tok…b4N` | `Authorization: token ghp…b4N` |
| `Authorization: CustomScheme f3a9c2e1…c4b8d3e5` | `Authorization: Cus…3e5` | `Authorization: CustomScheme f3a…3e5` |
| `{"Authorization":"token ghp_…"}` | `{"Authorization":"tok…b4N"}` | `{"Authorization":"token ghp…b4N"}` |
| `Authorization: Digest username="alice", realm="api", nonce="f3a9…", response="f3a9…"` | `Authorization: Dig…me="alice", realm="api", nonce="f3a…3e5", response="f3a…3e5"` | `Authorization: Digest username="alice", realm="api", nonce="f3a…3e5", response="f3a…3e5"` |

`inspect()` for the first row: `authorization[15,65]` and `context[15,65]` cover `token ghp_…`, while `github[21,65]` covers only the credential. For Digest: `authorization[15,31]` = `Digest username=`.

Script (library only, synthetic values): [experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3739-dd36d9843cea/experiments/issue-3739-upstream-repros.mjs), keys `authorizationScheme` and `digestAuthorization`.

## Cause

`authorizationRange` in `src/context.js` computes `tokenStart` after the optional scheme, but returns `{ start, end }` with `start` before the scheme. For Digest the token loop stops at the `"` delimiter right after `username=`.

## Suggested fix

- Return `{ start: tokenStart, end }` so the scheme stays visible for every scheme word (`token`, `Bearer`, `Basic`, `ApiKey`, custom ones), in `Authorization` and `Proxy-Authorization`, plain and in JSON.
- Treat `Digest` parameters as `key="value"` pairs: keep `username`, `realm`, `uri`, `qop`, `algorithm` and mask `response`, `nonce`/`cnonce`/`opaque` values (or at least do not mask the scheme and the `username=` key).
- Add the rows above to the tests.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.3 placeholder mode: second pass throws, [REDACTED] leftovers, generic ProperName labels, special-category leaks, no exported namespace, 2x cost
body:
Version: 0.19.3 (npm). Policy used in every example unless stated:

```js
createSyncSanitizer({
  profile: 'documents',
  properNames: 'capitalized',
  strict: true,
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: false, credentials: true },
});
```

Use case: application logs that must hold no personal data in the legal sense (152-FZ, GDPR incl. art. 9 special categories) yet stay readable for debugging, so `Person-1`, `Phone-1`, `Organization-1` are preferred over `[REDACTED]` and over length-only masks. Logs are sanitized more than once (in-process, then again when container output is collected). All values below are synthetic.

### 1. A second pass over placeholder output throws

```
first:  "Звонила Анна Смирнова, тел. +7 916 123-45-67" -> "ProperName-1 Person-1, тел. Phone-1"
second: sanitize("ProperName-1 Person-1, тел. Phone-1") -> throws ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION
second: sanitize("ProperName-1 Person-1, тел. Phone-1; перезвонил Пётр Сидоров") -> throws ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION
```

Expected: an opt-in such as `transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', existing: 'keep' }` that leaves tokens of the namespace as they are and numbers new values after the highest kept number per type, giving `ProperName-1 Person-1, тел. Phone-1; перезвонил Person-2`. Re-running placeholder mode on its own output should be idempotent; today every caller with a multi-stage pipeline has to write this themselves.

### 2. Placeholder mode still emits `[REDACTED]`

```
structured json, sensitiveFields: ['notes']
{"notes":"любой текст"}   -> {"notes":"[REDACTED]"}
{"age":34,"msg":"ok"}     -> {"age":"[REDACTED]","msg":"ok"}
```

Expected `Notes-1`/`Sensitive-1` and `Age-1` (prose already yields `Age-1` for `30 лет`).

### 3. Labels and boundaries under `properNames: 'capitalized'`

```
"Здравствуйте! Я Анна Смирнова, готова выйти"            -> "ProperName-1! ProperName-2 Person-1, готова выйти"
"Меня зовут Анна Смирнова"                                -> "ProperName-1 зовут Person-1"
"Работал в ООО «Ромашка», живу в Казани"                  -> "ProperName-1 в ProperName-2 ProperName-3, живу в ProperName-4"
"Кандидат Петров Иван Сергеевич, тел. +7 916 123-45-67"   -> "Person-1, тел. Phone-1"
"Иванов Иван Петрович работал в Лютике, позвонил Иванову" -> "Person-1 работал в ProperName-1, позвонил Person-2"
structured json {"url":"Меня зовут Анна Смирнова, тел. +7 916 123-45-67"} -> {"url":"Phone-1"}
```

- Sentence-initial common words (`Здравствуйте`, `Я`, `Меня`, `Работал`, `Звонила`) are replaced; the cue word `Кандидат` is absorbed into `Person-1`. Nothing personal would leak if they stayed, and a reader loses the sentence.
- `ООО` is split from the quoted name; the employer after `работал в` and the city after `живу в` are typed `ProperName`, though the cues say `Organization` / `Location`.
- `Иванову` is `Person-1` after `Иванов Иван` but `Person-2` after `Иванов Иван Петрович`: oblique forms of a known surname should link to the same number.
- Under a key named `url`, a prose value is replaced whole and typed `Phone`.

### 4. Special categories left in prose (strict)

21 of 42 synthetic rows keep the word:

```
узбечка по национальности | он узбек | таджик по национальности | чеченец | грузинка по национальности
азербайджанец, 30 лет | цыганка | кореянка по происхождению | he is Uzbek | протестант
перенес инсульт | шизофрения | слабослышащий | передвигается на коляске, колясочник | аутизм
wheelchair user | бисексуал | трансгендер | сидел за кражу | член профсоюза | trade union member
```

Related forms are caught (`татарка`, `мусульманка`, `лесбиянка`, `has HIV`, `имеет судимость`), so this looks like vocabulary coverage, not a missing rule.

### 5. Callers cannot extend the special-category vocabulary

`vocabulary` accepts `roles`, `organizationCues`, `educationCues`, `personalLabels` and `personalFields`. There is no list for strict attribute words, so the only extension point is `knownPersonal` with `compileKnown([{ type: 'PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTE', value: 'узбечка' }, ...])`. That works (`по национальности узбечка` -> `по национальности PersonalAttribute-1`), but it means maintaining exact word forms instead of extending the stem list the strict rule already uses. Expected: `vocabulary.personalAttributes` (or similar) feeding the same strict rule.

### 6. The placeholder namespace is not exported

To implement (1) outside the library a caller must know which `Type-n` tokens the library reserves. `reservedPlaceholderTypes`, `placeholderToken` and `catalogTypes` are internal, so the caller copies the native list and re-derives the vendor catalog types from `entityCatalogs`, which breaks silently when a type is added. Expected: export the reserved type list (or a `isPlaceholderToken(text)` helper).

### 7. Placeholder mode doubles per-call cost

```
"request completed in 12 ms", 100 calls: redact 2.05 ms/call, placeholder 4.19 ms/call
```

A CPU profile of a short line shows `preparePlaceholderText` at ~18% of `sanitize`: it rebuilds the namespace pattern from every reserved type (`placeholderToken` per type, then `new RegExp`) on every call. With `map: false` and no `knownPersonal` changes the pattern is constant per sanitizer and could be compiled once in `createSyncSanitizer`.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: We should update our list of competitors and make sure we support highest quality of all their features
body:
We should update list of competitors (open-source and closed-source) which have similar features, we should take all their best test cases and cases described in docs (if no source code provided), and make sure we also are able to support all of them in the best possible way.

So as result we will have comparison documentation with comparison with each competitor by supported features (on high level), and also pages with detailed support for all the features in detail.

So we and our user clearly understand actual state of things.

So our system is the most feature reach and reliable on the market for all the features we have. We also should support wide range of configuration options, as well as provide best possible class of extensibility/replacability of implementations and so on.

We should also check that we fully apply https://raw.githubusercontent.com/link-foundation/code-architecture-principles/refs/heads/main/README.md so it will be easier to maintain and use our system in the future.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.2 strict: special-category forms stay; disabled/single/man/russian over-redacted in operational text
body:
Found on 0.19.2 with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true`. All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const policy = { profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true };
const text = createSyncSanitizer(policy);
const json = createSyncSanitizer({ ...policy, structured: 'json' });
```

## 1. Special-category attributes that stay (`strict`)

`strict-attribute` lists a few fixed forms (`инвалидность`, `татарин`, `православный`, `мусульманин`, `диабет`, `ВИЧ`, `судимость`, `disabled`, `diabetic` …). Other forms of the same categories stay, both in text and in a JSON string value. These are special categories in 152-FZ art. 10 and GDPR art. 9: health, disability, ethnicity, religion, intimate life and criminal record.

| input | output (text and json `{"note": …}`) | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `кандидат инвалид` | unchanged | `инвалид` replaced |
| `является инвалидом 2 группы` | unchanged | `инвалидом` replaced |
| `по национальности армянин` | unchanged | `армянин` replaced |
| `она еврейка` | unchanged | `еврейка` replaced |
| `он казах` | unchanged | `казах` replaced |
| `христианин, верующий` | unchanged | `христианин` replaced |
| `исповедует ислам` | unchanged | `ислам` replaced |
| `иудей` | unchanged | replaced |
| `болеет эпилепсией` | unchanged | `эпилепсией` replaced |
| `астма с детства` | unchanged | `астма` replaced |
| `перенес онкологию` | unchanged | `онкологию` replaced |
| `туберкулез в анамнезе` | unchanged | `туберкулез` replaced |
| `на учете у психиатра` | unchanged | `психиатра` replaced |
| `депрессия, лечится` | unchanged | `депрессия` replaced |
| `гепатит C` | `гепатит [REDACTED]` (only `C`) | `гепатит` replaced |
| `нетрадиционная ориентация` | unchanged | replaced |
| `гей` | unchanged | replaced |
| `отбывал наказание` | unchanged | replaced |
| `epilepsy since 2010` | unchanged | `epilepsy` replaced |
| `is gay` | unchanged | `gay` replaced |
| `Armenian by birth` | unchanged | `Armenian` replaced |

Already replaced and should stay that way: `справка об инвалидности`, `инвалидность 3 группы`, `была судима`, `ВИЧ-инфицирован`, `беременность 20 недель`, `has a disability`, `candidate is diabetic`.

A fixed word list will keep missing forms: Russian inflects every noun and adjective, and the categories are open (any nationality, any diagnosis). Possible directions: match by stem with Russian case endings (`инвалид\p{L}{0,3}`), add a category lexicon (nationalities, religions, ICD chapter names) with endings, or a cue-based rule (`по национальности X`, `болеет X`, `на учете у X`, `исповедует X`).

## 2. Over-redaction of operational English (`strict`)

Some `strict-attribute` words are common in log and status text with no personal meaning. They are replaced in prose and as a whole JSON value:

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `the module is disabled` | `the module is [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `feature flag disabled for vacancy` | `feature flag [REDACTED] for vacancy` | unchanged |
| `single run finished` | `[REDACTED] run finished` | unchanged |
| `single-flight lock acquired` | `[REDACTED]-flight lock acquired` | unchanged |
| `retry on a single worker` | `retry on a [REDACTED] worker` | unchanged |
| `man page missing` | `[REDACTED] page missing` | unchanged |
| `locale russian selected` | `locale [REDACTED] selected` | unchanged |
| `asian region endpoint` | `[REDACTED] region endpoint` | unchanged |
| `{"status":"disabled"}` (json) | `{"status":"[REDACTED]"}` | unchanged |
| `{"status":"single"}` (json) | `{"status":"[REDACTED]"}` | unchanged |
| `{"status":"Russian"}` (json) | `{"status":"[REDACTED]"}` | unchanged |

Callers can't fix this: `detectors` only add findings, and turning off `strict-attribute` loses the whole category. Possible fixes: require a person cue for the ambiguous English words (`disabled`, `single`, `man`, `men`, `russian`, `asian`), for example a pronoun, `is a`, `candidate`, or a personal label before it. Or skip them right after a technical noun (`module`, `feature`, `flag`, `run`, `worker`, `lock`, `locale`, `region`), or before `-flight`/`page`. A way to keep listed words would also do (an `allowedValues`-style option, the opposite of `knownPersonal`).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.1 strict: lowercase ms/dr read as honorifics; compound personal keys stay
body:
Found on 0.19.1 with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true`. All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const policy = { profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true };
const text = createSyncSanitizer(policy);
const json = createSyncSanitizer({ ...policy, structured: 'json' });
```

## 1. A lowercase `ms` or `dr` before a capitalized word is read as an honorific

The new `document-person-cue` rule (#123) matches `[Mm]s\.?` and `[Dd]r\.?`. In logs, a lowercase `ms` is almost always the millisecond unit, and the next word is often a capitalized log word.

| input | 0.19.0 | 0.19.1 | expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `took 30 ms Retry scheduled` | unchanged | `took 30 ms [REDACTED] scheduled` | unchanged |
| `p95 120 ms Upstream healthy` | unchanged | `p95 120 ms [REDACTED] healthy` | unchanged |
| `{"msg":"took 30 ms Retry scheduled"}` (json) | unchanged | `Retry` replaced | unchanged |
| `see dr Drive mount` | unchanged | `dr [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `dr Who` | unchanged | `dr [REDACTED]` | unchanged |

These already work as expected and should keep working: `Ms. Smith`, `Ms Smith`, `Dr. Smith`, `Dr Smith`, `Mr. Brown`, `took 30 ms retry` and `12ms Retry`.

Possible fix: accept the honorifics `Ms`, `Mr`, `Dr` only when capitalized, or skip `ms` right after a number. A lowercase `mr`/`ms`/`dr` before a name is rare in English prose.

## 2. Compound personal keys that end in a known personal field stay (`structured: 'json'`)

0.19.1 replaces `displayName`, `fullName` and `originalFileName`, but not a compound key that ends in one of them:

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"recruiterDisplayName":"Olga"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"authorFullName":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"resumePdfOriginalFileName":"Petrov_Ivan_CV.pdf"}` | unchanged | value replaced |

`sensitiveFields` covers these per caller, so this is lower priority. A suffix match on the explicit field list (`…DisplayName`, `…FullName`, `…OriginalFileName`) would catch them by default and still leave a bare `name` alone.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: documents strict: bare Yandex Cloud keys, Latin names under personal keys and in English prose stay
body:
Found on `main` after #121 (and on 0.19.0) with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true`. All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const policy = { profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true };
const text = createSyncSanitizer(policy);
const json = createSyncSanitizer({ ...policy, structured: 'json' });
```

`X40` below stands for 40 mixed-case token characters such as `aB3_xY9kaB3_xY9k…`.

## 1. Bare Yandex Cloud credentials stay

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AQVN` + 36 token chars (API key) | unchanged | replaced |
| `key AQVN` + 36 token chars | unchanged | replaced |
| `t1.` + payload + `.` + 86 token chars (IAM token) | unchanged | replaced |
| `YCAJE` + 20 token chars (static key id) | unchanged | replaced |
| `YC` + 38 token chars (static key secret) | unchanged | replaced |

With a label such as `Authorization: Api-Key …` or `iam_token=…` they are replaced. The prefixes are documented and fixed, like `sk-ant-` or `ghp_`, which are already recognized bare.

## 2. One Latin word, a Latin file name or a number under a personal key stays (`structured: 'json'`)

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"candidateName":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"candidate_name":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"displayName":"Petrov"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"originalFileName":"Petrov_Ivan_CV.pdf"}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"age":34}` | unchanged | value replaced |
| `{"birthYear":1991}` | unchanged | value replaced |

`{"candidateName":"Петров"}` gives `{"candidateName":"[REDACTED]"}`, so only the Latin form is missing. `vocabulary.personalFields` holds `firstname`, `lastname`, `middlename` and `patronymic`. Compound keys that end in `name` (`candidateName`, `displayName`, `fullName`), `age` and `birthYear` look like they belong to the same group. A bare `name` is ambiguous (it also names jobs and products), so it can stay.

## 3. Latin names in English prose stay

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidate Ivan replied` | unchanged | `candidate [REDACTED] replied` |
| `Dear John,` | unchanged | `Dear [REDACTED],` |
| `Mr. Brown called` | unchanged | `Mr. [REDACTED] called` |
| `message from Ivan: ok` | unchanged | `message from [REDACTED]: ok` |

`Ivan Petrov replied` gives `[REDACTED] replied`, so two words are caught and one is not. `scripts: ['Cyrillic', 'Latin']` catches these, but it also replaces ordinary capitalized English words: `Request Failed: POST /api` gives `[REDACTED] Failed: [REDACTED] /api`. The optional `/ner` recognizer does not catch the single-word forms either. A person cue before a capitalized Latin word (`candidate`, `recruiter`, `applicant`, `Dear`, `Hi`, `Mr`, `Ms`, `Dr`) would cover the first three without the Latin script's false positives.

## Expected

Each row replaced, with tests, and English text without a person cue left as it is (`Request Failed: POST /api`, `Candidate Stage changed`).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: 0.19.0 strict: obfuscated emails, military ID numbers and lowercase employers stay; durations replaced as ages
body:
Found on 0.19.0 with `profile: 'documents'`, `properNames: 'capitalized'`, `strict: true` (plain text and `structured: 'json'` give the same results). All values below are synthetic.

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const s = createSyncSanitizer({ profile: 'documents', properNames: 'capitalized', strict: true });
s.sanitize(input).text;
```

## Kept (false negatives)

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ivan [at] example [dot] org` | unchanged | the address replaced |
| `ivan (at) example (dot) org` | unchanged | the address replaced |
| `ivan собака example.org` | `ivan собака [REDACTED]` | the local part replaced too |
| `пишите ivan[at]example.org` | `пишите ivan[at][REDACTED]` | the local part replaced too |
| `военный билет АБ 1234567` | `военный билет [REDACTED] 1234567` | the number replaced (the series alone is replaced now) |
| `работал в ромашке три года` | unchanged | the lowercase employer after `работал в` replaced |
| `Ромашка: менеджер` | unchanged | a capitalized Cyrillic word before a colon replaced when the text holds data and the word is not a known label (`Опыт`, `Стаж`, ...) |

`ivan at example dot org` is replaced, so the bracketed and `собака` forms look like missing variants of the same rule.

## Replaced (false positives under `strict`)

Without `strict` these durations stay, as fixed in #87. With `strict` they are replaced as ages:

| input | output | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Стаж: 5 лет` | `Стаж: [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `работал там 5 лет` | `работал там [REDACTED]` | unchanged |
| `Kubernetes (5 лет)` | `[REDACTED] ([REDACTED])` | `[REDACTED] (5 лет)` (the capitalized word is expected with `properNames`) |

`опыт работы 10 лет` stays under `strict`, so a duration cue (`стаж`, `работал`, a parenthesised skill) could take the same path. An age stays replaced: `кандидату 34 года`, `мне 34 года`, `возраст 41`.

## Expected

The kept forms replaced and the durations left as they are under `strict`, with tests for each row.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Strict profile for sensitive attributes and ambiguous bare values
body:
## Problem

These stay on 0.17.1, and a default profile is right to be careful, because each is ambiguous without context. Stored logs need the opposite tradeoff, where losing a date is cheap and keeping a person's data is not.

### Sensitive attributes with no label

- `женщина`
- `мужчина`
- `замужем`
- `женат, двое детей`
- `двое детей`
- `русская`
- `православный`
- `инвалидность 2 группы`
- `беременна`
- `судимость погашена`
- `член партии`

Labelled forms already work: `Пол: женский` gives `Пол: [REDACTED]` and `национальность: татарин` gives `национальность: [REDACTED]`.

### Bare values with no label

- `34 года`
- `12.03.1991`
- `12 марта 1991`
- `1991-03-12`
- `45 10 123456`
- `4510123456`
- `9161234567`
- `125009`

## Expected

An opt-in profile or option for stored logs, for example `profile: 'documents', strict: true`. Under it, these are replaced:

- health, religion, ethnicity, criminal record, political and family attributes, in Russian and English, in their common word forms;
- standalone ages, calendar dates in prose, passport-shaped and phone-shaped digit groups, and postal codes.

Dates and numbers in structural positions stay. That means ISO timestamps with a time part, values under fields declared with `structuralFields`, and numeric JSON values.

## Must stay under the strict option

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `опыт работы 10 лет` | `опыт работы 10 лет` |
| `Стаж 5 лет` | `Стаж 5 лет` |
| `2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z` | `2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z` |
| `request took 9161234567 ns` | `request took 9161234567 ns` |
| `Дети: нет` | `Дети: нет` |

`опыт работы 10 лет` shows the hard case: a duration and an age have the same shape. If it can't be separated reliably, the docs should say which way the option goes.

## Acceptance

- With the option on, every listed row is replaced and every control stays.
- With it off, nothing changes.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Reusable compiled known values for per-record use
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` is the most reliable route to high coverage, because it matches the value rather than its shape. It's case-insensitive and handles Russian forms:

| Known value | Type | Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `работал в ромашка` | `работал в [REDACTED]` |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `работал в Ромашке` | `работал в [REDACTED]` |
| `Ромашка` | ORGANIZATION | `Ромашка: менеджер` | `[REDACTED]: менеджер` |
| `МГУ` | EDUCATION | `окончил мгу` | `окончил [REDACTED]` |
| `Тверь` | LOCATION | `Живу в Твери` | `Живу в [REDACTED]` |

Using it in a log path means passing a list for each record or request, and the cost grows with the list on every call. On a 1 KB line on one laptop, with no other tuning: no list about 8.9 ms, 10 values 9.4 ms, 30 values 10.2 ms, 100 values 13.6 ms, 500 values 67 ms. The tail is what makes larger lists impractical on a hot path.

There's also no documented answer to two questions:

- Which `type` values change behaviour? Any uppercase string appears to be accepted.
- Which values match across formats? A date and a phone number do. A link only matches with its scheme: with `https://example.org/anna` known, `example.org/anna` gives `example.org/anna`, and `https://example.org/anna?x=1` gives `[REDACTED]?x=1`.

## Expected

```js
const known = compileKnown([{ type: 'ORGANIZATION', value: 'Ромашка' }]);
sanitize(line, { profile: 'documents', knownPersonal: known });
```

- A compiled list can be reused and merged, and it doesn't hold anything beyond what the caller passed.
- `docs/API.md` lists the types and what each one matches, across formats and word forms.

## Acceptance

- With a compiled list of 500 values, cost per call stays within 10% of no list, plus the matching itself.
- A known link also matches without its scheme, and its query string and trailing slash are replaced with it.
- Output is the same as with a plain array.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Offline in-process recognition for names with no cue
body:
## Problem

Pattern rules can't recognize an organization, school or place with no cue, and `minConfidence` doesn't help, because `inspect` returns no finding at all for these:

- `Работал в Ромашке менеджером.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `Worked at Romashka for three years.`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `graduated from MSU`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `MIT, 2012`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0
- `at Romashka`: output unchanged, also with `minConfidence: 0`, inspect finds 0

`docs/COVERAGE.md` points to the Presidio bridge for this. It's a subprocess with a Python model, so it can't run in a synchronous log hook and is a heavy dependency for a JavaScript service.

## Expected

An optional, offline, in-process recognizer for person, organization, school and location names in Russian and English, for example a small ONNX or WASM model loaded by a separate entry point:

```js
import { createNerDetector } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/ner';
const detector = await createNerDetector({ languages: ['ru', 'en'] });
```

- It's a separate optional dependency, with no download at analysis time.
- Once loaded it can run synchronously, or the docs state how to run it from a worker when it can't.
- `docs/COVERAGE.md` publishes precision and recall per type and language, with the test set.

## Acceptance

- The rows above are replaced with the detector on.
- `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL`, `Встреча в понедельник` and operational English stay.
- Cost per kilobyte is published. With the detector off, nothing changes in size or speed.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Custom transformation callback and a synchronous engine interface
body:
## Problem

Replacements come from a closed list of modes:

```js
sanitize('Анна Смирнова', { profile: 'documents', transformation: (finding) => 'Z' });
// throws ERR_CONFIG
```

The stream and outbound APIs accept a custom `sanitizer`, which is a clean way to swap the engine. Both are async, and `sanitize()` has no equivalent, so swapping an implementation in a synchronous path means rebuilding it around the library.

The stages are partly there already. `inspect()` detects, `redact()` replaces with no verification, and `knownOnly` with `findings` replaces with verification:

```js
sanitize('Ромашка, Анна Смирнова, a@b.example', { profile: 'documents', knownOnly: true, findings: [{ start: 0, end: 7, category: 'personal', type: 'ORGANIZATION', rule: 'x' }] }).text;
// "[REDACTED], Анна Смирнова, a@b.example"
```

The `knownOnly` row in `docs/API.md` mentions known values and reused maps but not `findings`, so this isn't described as a supported way to replace detection.

## Expected

1. `transformation` and `transformations[type]` accept a function `(finding) => string`. The result goes through residual verification, and a throw blocks output.
2. Documented stages, each with a stated contract: detect, merge, transform, verify.
3. A `SyncSanitizer` interface with `inspect` and `sanitize`, plus a documented recipe for replacing detection while keeping verification.

## Acceptance

- A function transformation works in text and structured modes, and a result that still holds the original value is blocked.
- Passing a Promise-returning function throws `ERR_CONFIG` in synchronous calls.
- Existing modes don't change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: sensitiveFields: case styles, nested paths and an allow-list mode
body:
## Problem

`sensitiveFields` only matches one exact spelling at any depth, while built-in personal field names match in any case style.

| Input | `sensitiveFields` | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"fooBar":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `{"foo_bar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"foo_bar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"FooBar":"Значение"}` | `["fooBar"]` | `{"FooBar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` | `["foobar"]` | `{"fooBar":"Значение"}` |
| `{"a":{"b":"Значение"}}` | `["a.b"]` | `{"a":{"b":"Значение"}}` |
| `{"x":"Значение"}` | `["*"]` | `{"x":"Значение"}` |

A value logged alone under a neutral key has nothing to recognize, whatever the detectors do:

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `{"note":"1991-03-12"}` | `{"note":"1991-03-12"}` |
| `{"note":"Romashka"}` | `{"note":"Romashka"}` |
| `{"note":"https://example.org/cv/abc123def"}` | `{"note":"https://example.org/cv/abc123def"}` |

The only complete answer for such values is to name the fields that are safe to keep.

## Expected

1. Names match in any case style by default, the same as built-in field names. `exactFields` keeps today's behaviour.
2. Dotted paths and `*` work: `a.b`, `items.*.name`.
3. A new option, `allowedFields`: in JSON and JSONL, string values under any other key become `[REDACTED]`. Values under listed keys are still scanned. Numbers and booleans are unaffected.

## Acceptance

- The table rows behave as above.
- `allowedFields: ['msg', 'level']` on `{"msg":"ok","note":"Romashka"}` gives `{"msg":"ok","note":"[REDACTED]"}`.
- Output stays valid JSON with the same keys and numbers.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Let callers extend the document vocabulary
body:
## Problem

The documents profile depends on closed lists: role words, organization cues, school cues, label names and personal field names. They can't be extended. `document-vocabulary.js` isn't exported, and a deep import fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Every miss therefore needs an upstream release.

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `группа компаний Ромашка` | `группа компаний Ромашка` |
| `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` | `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` |
| `стартап Ромашка` | `стартап Ромашка` |

Only the first word of the entry decides the first two rows. A caller who knows their domain could add `маркетолог` in one line.

## Expected

```js
sanitize(text, {
  profile: 'documents',
  vocabulary: {
    roles: ['маркетолог'],
    organizationCues: ['группа компаний', 'стартап'],
    educationCues: ['обучение'],
    personalLabels: ['личный контакт'],
    personalFields: ['contactPerson'],
  },
});
```

- The additions extend the built-in lists. A `replace: true` form swaps a list out entirely.
- Bad entries throw `ERR_CONFIG`.
- Lists are normalized the same way as the built-in ones, so case and Russian word forms behave alike.
- The built-in lists are exported read-only, so a caller can see what's already covered.

## Acceptance

- With `roles: ['маркетолог']`, the first row gives the same output as the second.
- With no `vocabulary`, output doesn't change.
- The cost stays bounded, and repeated calls with the same vocabulary don't recompile it each time.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Per-rule and per-type control over built-in detection
body:
## Problem

Built-in rules can't be switched off or narrowed one at a time, so an over-redaction or a noisy rule has no fix on the caller's side. What exists today doesn't cover it:

| Attempt | Result on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `sanitize(s, { rules: { person: false } })` | throws ERR_CONFIG (no such option) |
| `{"location":"apps/api"}` with `structuralFields: ['location']` | `{"location":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `Работала в компании Ромашка` with `documentEntities: false` | `Работала в компании [REDACTED]` |
| `Работала в компании Ромашка` with no options at all | `Работала в компании [REDACTED]` |

The last two rows look like a bug: `docs/API.md` says `documentEntities: false` turns document recognizers off and that they are off by default, yet this cue still fires. `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)` does follow the flag.

`publicEntities` can exempt one exact value, but it needs a source and a review date per value, so it doesn't suit a class of false positives such as technology names.

## Expected

- Rule ids in `Finding.rule` are documented and stable.
- `rules: { '<id>': false }` turns off one rule, and an unknown id throws `ERR_CONFIG`.
- `types: { ORGANIZATION: false }` turns off one type.
- Credential rules can't be turned off this way unless the caller also sets an explicit, separately named option.
- A way to exempt a built-in field name, for example `fields: { location: 'scan' }`, so the value is scanned as ordinary text rather than replaced whole.
- `documentEntities: false` turns off every document recognizer, or the docs say which ones stay.

## Acceptance

- Each row above has a documented way to get the opposite result.
- With no new option set, output doesn't change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: sanitize() accepts detectors and does nothing; allow synchronous detectors
body:
## Problem

Unknown options fail closed with `ERR_CONFIG`, so a typo can't turn protection off. `detectors` is the exception: the synchronous `sanitize()` and `inspect()` accept it and do nothing. A comment in `index.d.ts` says synchronous functions use native rules only, but the call raises no error, so a caller who misses the comment believes the detector runs.

```js
const detector = { detect: (t) => { const i = t.indexOf('Ромашка'); return i < 0 ? [] : [{ start: i, end: i + 7, category: 'personal', type: 'ORGANIZATION', rule: 'x', confidence: 1 }]; } };
sanitize('Ромашка тут', { profile: 'documents', detectors: [detector] }).text;
// "Ромашка тут"
(await createSanitizer({ profile: 'documents', detectors: [detector], secretlint: false }).sanitize('Ромашка тут')).text;
// "[REDACTED] тут"
```

A log hook has to be synchronous, so it can't use `createSanitizer`. Today the only synchronous route is to run your own detection and pass `findings` to `sanitize()`. That works, but it means every caller rebuilds the detector loop, and `structured: 'json'` needs offsets into the serialized text.

## Expected

1. `sanitize()` and `inspect()` run detectors whose `detect` returns an array, on the same inputs as the async engine, including each string value in structured mode.
2. A detector returning a Promise throws `ERR_CONFIG` in synchronous calls instead of being skipped.
3. The types and `docs/API.md` say the same.

## Acceptance

- The example above gives `[REDACTED] тут` from both engines.
- In `structured: 'json'` a detector sees decoded string values, and its offsets refer to them.
- A detector that throws blocks output, as it does in the async engine.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required
