title: Option to replace proper names in prose that has no cue
body:
## Problem

The `documents` profile recognises organizations, schools and places by cues. Prose with no cue keeps them, and no list of cues can cover it:

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` | `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` |
| `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.` | `Ромашка: менеджер, 3 года.` |
| `Сотрудник работал в Romashka три года.` | `Сотрудник работал в Romashka три года.` |
| `Живу в Твери` | `Живу в Твери` |

This matters most for stored logs, where text is kept only for diagnosis and losing a few extra words costs little. Generated text that quotes a document is the worst case: on a private set of CV-shaped documents, a caller-side rule took kept organization names from 57% to under 1% in generated prose, and from 26% to 2% in the documents themselves.

## Request

An option that replaces anything shaped like a proper name, in text that a caller marks as prose. For example:

```js
sanitize(text, { profile: "documents", properNames: "capitalized" });
```

## Suggested behaviour

The rule that gave those numbers, as a starting point. It is structural and has no word lists.

Apply it to a string value only when the value holds data, meaning any of:

- a letter from a script other than the caller's operational language (a `scripts: ["Cyrillic"]` setting, for example)
- a parenthesized date range
- a comma-separated mobile number
- a link with a `/d/<id>` path

Then replace:

- any word with an uppercase letter anywhere in it, including joined forms such as `Санкт-Петербург` or `A.B`
- text in typographic quotes, such as `«ромашка лютик»`
- links, including a bare `example.org/path`
- bare mobile numbers

Keep:

- `Label:`, meaning a capitalized word right before a colon
- lowercase words, numbers and dates
- path segments and JSON keys
- values that do not hold data, byte for byte

| Input | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` | `[REDACTED] в [REDACTED] менеджером по продажам.` |
| `Опыт: работал в Ромашке 5 лет` | `Опыт: работал в [REDACTED] 5 лет` |
| `Маркетолог, ГК «ромашка лютик» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `[REDACTED], [REDACTED] [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Founder, consultant, Romashka (2019-2021)` | `[REDACTED], consultant, [REDACTED] (2019-2021)` |
| `Connection to Postgres lost, retrying` | unchanged |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | unchanged |
| `Window Closed (2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z)` | unchanged |

## Known limits of the rule

- An organization written in lowercase stays.
- `Ромашка: менеджер` stays, because it looks like a label.
- An English value with no such shape stays, for example `Worked at Romashka for three years.`
- A personal website root in such a value stays, for example `https://anna-smirnova.example.org/`
- A value logged alone under a neutral key with no shape stays, for example `{"note":"Romashka"}` or `{"note":"1991-03-12"}`

## Acceptance

- The option is off by default, so existing output doesn't change.
- Running it twice gives the same result as running it once.
- JSON stays valid, with the same keys and numbers.
- Cost stays linear in input length, including long tokens with no spaces.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: documents profile 0.17.0: employers stay in dated lines with unlisted titles or a lead-in; comma phones and school forms
body:
## Summary

Checked 0.17.0 from npm after #94 and #91 closed. Everything reported there is fixed or documented, thank you. The forms below still leave personal data in text mode and in `structured: 'json'`. On a private set of CVs, employers in dated experience lines are most of what is still kept, and the kept rate did not change between 0.16.2 and 0.17.0. All values here are invented.

```js
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
```

## Dated experience lines

### 1. The title has to start with a listed word

`role` in `src/document-extras.js` lists 12 words. A line with the same structure is handled only if its title starts with one of them, while the date range is what anchors the entry:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (Лютик) (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка (Лютик) (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Romashka, LLC (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |
| `Маркетолог, Romashka, LLC (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог, Ромашка / Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Основатель, консультант, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог (B2B), Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |

### 2. Text before the entry

`role.test(parts[0])` is anchored to the start of the prefix, so a lead-in such as `Опыт:` stops a listed title from matching:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Опыт: директор, основатель, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Опыт работы: Менеджер, консультант, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Опыт: менеджер (b2b), Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Стаж = 5 лет: Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `= 3 года, Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Лютик (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01). Директор, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01). Директор, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |

### 3. Other employer shapes

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Менеджер, Ромашка \| маркетинг, продажи (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка Лютик \| IT, связь (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Маркетолог, ГК «Ромашка Лютик» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `ГК «Ромашка» (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |

## Bare mobile number after a comma

`контакт: 89161234567` is now replaced. These are not:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Анна, 89161234567` | unchanged |
| `Письмо, 89161234567, жду ответа` | unchanged |
| `Иванова А., 79161234567, Москва` | `[REDACTED], 79161234567, [REDACTED]` |

## School acronyms and names after brackets or other cues

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `(МГУ, 2012)` | unchanged |
| `Образование (МГУ)` | unchanged |
| `в МГТУ им. Баумана` | unchanged |
| `Обучение: Skillbox, 2020` | unchanged |

## Lower priority: over-redaction from the new company cues

This is the safe direction, but it costs readability, and these are technologies, not companies:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `опыт в Python и Go` | `опыт в [REDACTED] и [REDACTED]` |
| `опыт в SQL, Excel и Power BI` | `опыт в [REDACTED], [REDACTED] и [REDACTED]` |
| `Kubernetes (5 лет)` | `[REDACTED] (5 лет)` |
| `Python (2 года), Go (3 года)` | `[REDACTED] (2 года), [REDACTED] (3 года)` |
| `проекты для Telegram` | `проекты для [REDACTED]` |
| `Роль в Scrum: мастер` | `Роль в [REDACTED]: мастер` |

## Lower priority: cost

`organization-experience` and the cues add time on long lines: on one laptop, a 9 KB JSON line went from about 34 ms on 0.16.2 to about 72 ms on 0.17.0, on the main thread of a synchronous caller. A 267-byte line went from about 3.3 ms to 3.9 ms.

## Must stay unchanged

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Опыт: 3 года, 5 месяцев` | unchanged |
| `Директор, руководитель отдела` | unchanged |
| `Встреча, понедельник (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `Отпуск (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | unchanged |
| `id 79161234567` | unchanged |
| `Встреча в понедельник с Романом` | unchanged |
| `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL` | unchanged |

## Expected

1. A date range anchors an entry whatever word its title starts with, and whatever comes before the entry on the line. The employer is replaced in sections 1 to 3.
2. A Russian mobile number after a comma is replaced in document prose, without touching the `order` and `id` controls.
3. The school rows are replaced, or `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists them as limits.
4. Well-known technology names under the new cues stay, or the over-redaction is documented.

## Acceptance

- Every row in sections 1 to 3 and the phone section is replaced, in text and JSON mode.
- The "Must stay unchanged" rows stay unchanged.
- Tests use several titles outside the current list, not only the ones above, so the fix doesn't grow the list by these words alone.

comments.body:
Rechecked on 0.17.1: every row in this issue gives the same output as on 0.17.0, so nothing here has changed. Below are more cases found while drafting a caller-side workaround. All values are synthetic.

Each table shows real output.

| `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` | `Работал в Ромашке менеджером по продажам.` |

### Second item of a list after a cue

| --- | --- |
| `Анна работала в Лютике, потом в Ромашке.` | `Анна работала в [REDACTED], потом в Ромашке.` |

### English bare mobile

| --- | --- |
| `Anna, 89161234567` | `Anna, 89161234567` |
| `Letter, 89161234567, waiting for a reply` | `Letter, 89161234567, waiting for a reply` |

### Share links with a short id

| --- | --- |
| `https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNo/view?usp=sharing` | `https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNo/view?usp=sharing` |

### Over-redaction

| Input | Output on 0.17.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `Релиз, Kubernetes (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Релиз, [REDACTED] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` |


### Field names and values

- `{"location":"apps/api"}` with `{}` => `{"location":"[REDACTED]"}`
- `{"fooBar":"Иван"}` with `{"sensitiveFields":["fooBar"]}` => `{"fooBar":"[REDACTED]"}`
- `{"foo_bar":"Иван"}` with `{"sensitiveFields":["fooBar"]}` => `{"foo_bar":"Иван"}`
- `{"FooBar":"Иван"}` with `{"sensitiveFields":["fooBar"]}` => `{"FooBar":"Иван"}`

- `location` is replaced even when the value is a relative path. A value shaped like a relative path could stay.
- `sensitiveFields` matches only the exact spelling, while the built-in field names match in any case style. It would help if caller-supplied names were matched the same way.

### Expected

- Lowercase organizations: stay is acceptable only if documented, because they conflict with `Встреча, понедельник (...)`. Please state which way the profile goes.
- The English shapes should behave like their Russian equivalents.
- `ГК` and `группа компаний` should work as organization cues, with or without quotes.
- A list continuation after a cue, such as `в Лютике, потом в Ромашке`, should be replaced throughout.
- A comma-separated mobile number should be replaced in English text too.
- Links with a `/d/<id>` path should be replaced whatever the id length and host.
- `Релиз, Kubernetes (...)` is the safe direction, so it is low priority.

The no-cue prose rows are the subject of a separate request for an option, filed as a separate issue.

title: documents profile: remaining gaps from one full pass (experience lines, multi-word labels, field names, phones, share links, ERR_RESIDUAL)
body:
## Summary

I ran one full pass over the `documents` profile on `c5b61aa6` (main, after #90), using CV-shaped text and structured log lines, so everything missing can land in one release. All values below are invented. Issue #91 is still open, and its rows are not repeated here.

Releasing the `#90` fixes alone is not blocked by this issue. `Checks and release` failed on `c5b61aa6` at the step `Version packages and commit to main` (run 42060440016), so nothing from #90 is on npm yet: the latest version is still 0.16.1. I could not find the cause in the log.

## Setup

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
const json = (v) => sanitize(JSON.stringify(v), { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }).text;
```

The text rows behave the same way under `json({ note: s })`, so the same fix should cover both.

## 1. CV experience lines still keep the employer

This is the biggest remaining source of leaks in CV text. The rule works for `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)`, but not when the title or employer has more structure, when the end date is empty, or for the second entry on a line.

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Директор, руководитель отдела, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)` | unchanged |
| `Директор (продажи), Ромашка (2019 – 2021)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер / руководитель, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, ГК «Ромашка» (2019 – 2021)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, ООО (2019 – 2021)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка, Москва (2019 – 2021)` | `Менеджер, Ромашка, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021)` |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (Москва) (2019 – 2021)` | `Менеджер, Ромашка ([REDACTED]) (2019 – 2021)` |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-01-01 — )` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019-01-01 — null)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021); Директор, Лютик (2021 – 2023)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021); Директор, Лютик (2021 – 2023)` |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021), Директор, Лютик (2021 – 2023)` | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021), Директор, Лютик (2021 – 2023)` |
| `Ромашка, менеджер (2019-01-01 — 2021-05-31)` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер \| Ромашка \| 2019-01-01 — 2021-05-31` | unchanged |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка Лютик` | unchanged |
| `- Ромашка Лютик 5 лет` | unchanged |
| `Последнее место работы Ромашка Лютик` | unchanged |

The last three rows have no date to anchor on, and they look like `Директор, руководитель отдела` (a control below), so listing them as limits is fine.

## 2. A label replaces only the first word of the value

This is a partial leak: the output looks clean, but part of the name stays.

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Компания: Ромашка Лютик` | `Компания: [REDACTED] Лютик` |
| `Работодатель: Ромашка Лютик` | `Работодатель: [REDACTED] Лютик` |
| `Место работы: Ромашка Лютик, менеджер` | `Место работы: [REDACTED] Лютик, менеджер` |
| `Employer: Romashka Lyutik` | `Employer: [REDACTED] Lyutik` |
| `Company: Romashka Lyutik` | `Company: [REDACTED] Lyutik` |

`Компания: ООО Ромашка Лютик` is replaced in full, so the legal form seems to be what extends the match. Expected: the value is replaced up to the end of the line or the next comma.

## 3. Field names in structured mode

| field | value | output |
|---|---|---|
| `firstName` | `Анна` | unchanged |
| `lastName` | `Смирнова` | unchanged |
| `middleName` | `Викторовна` | unchanged |
| `middle_name` | `Викторовна` | unchanged |
| `patronymic` | `Викторовна` | unchanged |
| `birthday` | `1991-03-12` | unchanged |
| `birth_date` | `1991-03-12T00:00:00.000Z` | unchanged |
| `sex` | `F` | unchanged |
| `citizenship` | `Казахстан` | unchanged |
| `nationality` | `Казахстан` | unchanged |

| `employer` | `Ромашка` | unchanged |
| `university` | `КФУ` | unchanged |
| `school` | `Школа 5` | unchanged |
| `contact` | `89161234567` | unchanged |
| `resume_url` | `https://example.org/doc/abc` | unchanged |
| `resumeUrl` | `https://example.org/doc/abc` | unchanged |

| `profile_url` | `https://example.org/in/abc` | unchanged |
| `company_url` | `https://romashka.example.org` | unchanged |

The cases here that look inconsistent:

- `first_name` and `last_name` are replaced, but `firstName` and `lastName` are not.
- `birthDate` is replaced with the same ISO value, but `birth_date` is not. `birth_date` is replaced when the value is `1991-03-12`.
- An absolute URL is replaced under `url`, but not under other URL-named fields.

### Request: a caller-declared field list

Please add a counterpart to `structuralFields`, for example `sensitiveFields: string[]`, whose declared property names are always replaced in full by the synchronous `sanitize`. `detectors` only applies to `createSanitizer`, so a synchronous caller has no way to do this today.

This is the most useful single item here. Callers could cover their own field names and fields that hold free text without waiting for a release, and field-name gaps would stop needing new rules.

## 4. Phone numbers with no cue word

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `контакт: 89161234567` | unchanged |
| `пишите, 79161234567` | unchanged |
| `89161234567` | unchanged |

`звоните 89161234567` and `телефон для связи, 89161234567` are replaced, and so is `phone: 89161234567`, so the gap is the cue. Expected: `контакт:` counts as a label. For a bare 11-digit mobile number, please pick a rule and document it, keeping the controls below unchanged.

## 5. Share links and personal sites in text

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `портфолио https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTuVwXyZ012345/view?usp=sharing` | unchanged |
| `https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTuVwXyZ012345/edit` | unchanged |
| `https://example.org/s/9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e` | unchanged |
| `портфолио https://ivan-petrov.example.org/` | unchanged |

A long opaque path segment on a document host works as a capability link: anyone holding it can open the file. Expected: a long opaque segment is replaced, or the limit is listed in `docs/COVERAGE.md`. A personal site root cannot be told apart from any other site, so documenting it as a limit is fine.

## 6. Smaller text forms

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `С уважением,\nАнна` | unchanged |
| `учился в МГУ` | unchanged |
| `Соискатель: Абвгде Жзиклм` | unchanged |
| `Сотрудник: Абвгде Жзиклм` | unchanged |
| `ФИО: Абвгде Жзиклм` | `ФИО: [REDACTED]` |

The first row is a signature split across two lines, while `С уважением, Анна` is replaced. The second is a verb gap: `окончила КФУ (2015)` is replaced. The next two are role labels: `ФИО:` is replaced, so a value with an unlisted surname depends on the label list.

## 7. `ERR_RESIDUAL` on doubly escaped text in structured mode

```js
json({ output: '"\\",ООО\\\\\\"Р\\\\\\"\\""' }); // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
text('"\\",ООО\\\\\\"Р\\\\\\"\\""');         // "\",[REDACTED]\""
```

Model output that embeds JSON inside JSON can contain this form. Failing closed is safe, but the whole record is lost for one short fragment, when text mode handles the same input. Expected: the fragment is replaced and the record stays parseable.

## Must stay unchanged

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Опыт: 3 года, 5 месяцев` | unchanged |
| `Директор, руководитель отдела` | unchanged |
| `order 89161234567 shipped` | unchanged |
| `id 79161234567` | unchanged |
| `https://example.org/docs/getting-started` | unchanged |
| `https://github.com/` | unchanged |

## Acceptance

- Every row in sections 1, 2 and 4 is replaced, in text and structured modes, or `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists it as a limit.
- `sensitiveFields` (or an equivalent) works in the synchronous `sanitize`, and output stays parseable.
- Section 3 follows one documented rule for name variants and URL-named fields.
- Section 7 returns parseable output.
- The controls above stay byte-identical.
- A release containing #90 is published.

comments.body:
Rechecked on 0.16.2 from npm: every row in this issue reproduces unchanged. The note above saying the #90 fixes aren't on npm is out of date. They are released in 0.16.2, and those forms now behave correctly.

## One more case: company names in free text

This matters when free text is logged and the sanitizer is the only filter applied to it. All values are invented. `text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text`.

| input | 0.16.2 |
|---|---|
| `работал в «Ромашка»` | `работал в [REDACTED]` (correct) |
| `работал в Ромашка` | `работал в [REDACTED]` (correct) |
| `работал в компании «Ромашка Лютик»` | unchanged |
| `сильный опыт (Ромашка Лютик)` | unchanged |
| `опыт в Romashka и Lyutik` | unchanged |
| `Роль в Romashka: руководитель` | unchanged |
| `проекты для Ромашка, Лютик и Василек` | unchanged |
| `Romashka (2 года), Lyutik (3 года)` | unchanged |

These must stay unchanged:

- `Встреча в понедельник с Романом`
- `Использовал Kubernetes и PostgreSQL`

## Expected

1. Forms with a cue are replaced: `компании «…»`, a name after `опыт в` or `проекты для`, a list after such a cue, and a name followed by a duration such as `(2 года)`.
2. A name with no cue can't be told apart from an ordinary word by pattern alone. To cover it, callers need a synchronous way to add their own values or detectors. `detectors` applies only to `createSanitizer`; `sanitize` ignores it, so a synchronous caller, such as a log hook, can't add a detector today:

   ```js
   sanitize('Lyutik работал', {
     profile: 'documents',
     detectors: [{ id: 'x', detect: () => [{ start: 0, end: 6, type: 'ORG' }] }],
   }).text;
   // 'Lyutik работал'
   ```

   Either honouring `detectors` in `sanitize`, or a synchronous sanitizer instance, would solve this. If neither fits, please say so in `docs/COVERAGE.md`.

## Acceptance

- The cue rows above are replaced, and the two control rows stay unchanged.
- A caller of a synchronous API can add a detector or a list of values, or the limit is documented.

title: 0.16.1: percent-encoded emails and phones in URLs are kept, and /profile/ paths are only replaced under the url label
body:
## Summary

In the `documents` profile, an email or phone number in a URL query is kept when it is percent-encoded, and `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists percent as a supported decoding. The plain form of the same value is replaced. URL query strings are normally percent-encoded, so this is the common form in access logs.

Separately, a personal path such as `/profile/<id>` is replaced under the `url` label and kept under any other label or in plain text.

## Reproduction (0.16.1)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';

const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
const json = (v) =>
  sanitize(JSON.stringify(v), { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }).text;
```

All values are invented.

### Percent-encoded values

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/p?email=anna.smirnova@example.org' })` | `{"link":"https://example.org/p?email=[REDACTED]"}` (correct) |
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/p?email=anna.smirnova%40example.org' })` | unchanged |
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/p?phone=+79161234567' })` | `{"link":"https://example.org/p?phone=[REDACTED]"}` (correct) |
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/p?phone=%2B79161234567' })` | unchanged |
| `json({ target: '/login?email=anna.smirnova%40example.org' })` | unchanged |
| `text('GET /login?email=anna.smirnova%40example.org 200')` | unchanged |

A percent-encoded `name=` value in the same position is replaced, so only some labels are affected.

### Personal paths outside the `url` label

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/profile/abc123def' })` | unchanged |
| `json({ link: 'https://example.org/users/abc123def' })` | unchanged |

## Expected

- A percent-encoded email or phone number in a query gets the same result as its plain form.
- The personal-path rule used for `url` applies to URL values under other labels and in plain text, or `docs/COVERAGE.md` lists this as a known limit.

## Acceptance

- Each unchanged row above is replaced, or documented as a limit.
- URLs without personal data stay byte-identical.

comments.body:
Two smaller findings on `main` at `c5b61aa6` (unreleased), both with invented values.

| `json({ note: 'Дети: нет\nуровень: info' })` | `{"note":"Дети: [REDACTED]"}` | The field is kept when it is alone (`Дети: нет`), and in text mode with the same second line. In JSON it is replaced, and the later lines are removed with it. |

title: 0.16.1: durations are replaced as ages ('опыт работы [REDACTED] лет'), a stack frame is swallowed, and /u/ and /in/ paths are kept under url
body:
## Summary

Some rules added in 0.16.1 replace text that holds no personal data. These rows are unchanged in 0.16.0. The first group follows from my own report in #82, which listed a bare `34 года` as a miss without saying how to tell an age from a duration.

## Reproduction

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
const json = (v) => sanitize(JSON.stringify(v), { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }).text;
```

### Durations are replaced as ages

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `опыт работы 5 лет` | unchanged | `опыт работы [REDACTED] лет` |
| `стаж 12 лет` | unchanged | `стаж [REDACTED] лет` |
| `3 года опыта` | unchanged | `[REDACTED] года опыта` |
| `за последние 3 года` | unchanged | `за последние [REDACTED] года` |
| `более 10 лет` | unchanged | `более [REDACTED] лет` |
| `через 5 лет` | unchanged | `через [REDACTED] лет` |
| `договор на 3 года` | unchanged | `договор на [REDACTED] года` |
| `Проект длился 2 года` | unchanged | `Проект длился [REDACTED] года` |
| `Задача выполнена за 3 года` | unchanged | `Задача выполнена за [REDACTED] года` |

A number with `года` or `лет` is an age only with some sign of a person's age: a label (`возраст`), `мне`, `исполнилось`, or a gender word (`Женщина, 34 года`). `опыт`, `стаж`, `за`, `через`, `более` and `на` point to a duration. A bare `34 года` on its own is ambiguous, so keeping it and listing it as a limit would be fine.

### A stack frame after an address and port is replaced

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `{"stack":"Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432\n    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect (node:net:1595:16)"}` | unchanged | `{"stack":"Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432[REDACTED] (node:net:1595:16)"}` |

The newline and the frame's function name are replaced, so the stack trace loses its line break and its first frame. A stack without the address stays unchanged:

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `{"stack":"Error: boom\n    at f (/app/src/index.ts:10:5)\n    at async g (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)"}` | unchanged | unchanged |

### Words after a label that say nothing about the person

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `Гражданство: не указано` | unchanged | `Гражданство: [REDACTED]` |
| `Дети: нет` | unchanged | `Дети: [REDACTED]` |

`Пол: не указан` and `возраст: не указан` stay unchanged, so these two look inconsistent.

### Personal paths under `url` are now kept

This is the opposite problem: a miss that came with the relative-URL exemption from #79.

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `{"url":"/u/petr.kuz"}` | `{"url":"[REDACTED]"}` | unchanged |
| `{"url":"/in/petr-kuz"}` | `{"url":"[REDACTED]"}` | unchanged |

`/user/`, `/users/`, `/profile/`, `/member/`, `/home/` and `/people/` are still replaced.

### Also in 0.16.0: a listen address

| input | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `Server listening at http://0.0.0.0:3000` | `Server listening at http://[REDACTED]:3000` | `Server listening at http://[REDACTED]:3000` |

`http://localhost:3000/api/v1/items` stays unchanged, and so does `127.0.0.1` elsewhere.

## Expected

- A duration is not replaced as an age.
- A stack frame is kept, including its line break.
- `/u/<name>` and `/in/<name>` under `url` are replaced.

## Acceptance

- The rows above behave as described, and ages from #82 stay replaced (`мне 29 лет`, `возраст: 34`, `Женщина, 34 года`).

title: 0.16.1: structured json mode is 2.5x to 10x slower per call than 0.16.0 on lines with no personal data
body:
## Summary

`sanitize` with `profile: 'documents'` takes several times longer per call in 0.16.1 than in 0.16.0, on short lines with no personal data in them. This matters for callers that sanitize each log line synchronously as it is written: the time is spent on the main thread for every line.

## Reproduction (Node 24, Apple Silicon)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const line = JSON.stringify({"level":30,"time":1730000000000,"id":"req-1a","msg":"request completed","req":{"method":"GET","url":"/api/v1/items","route":"/api/v1/items/:id","host":"api.example.org","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":52344},"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":12.34});
for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) sanitize(line, { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }); // warm up
const start = performance.now();
for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) sanitize(line, { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' });
console.log((performance.now() - start) / 400, 'ms per call');
```

Median of 3 runs, after warm-up:

| line | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| short JSON line (100 chars) | 0.35 ms | 2.31 ms | 6.6x |
| longer JSON line (264 chars) | 0.52 ms | 5.61 ms | 10.8x |
| 9 KB JSON line (9453 chars) | 13.75 ms | 34.85 ms | 2.5x |
| longer line, text mode (264 chars) | 1.12 ms | 1.10 ms | 1.0x |

Text mode costs the same in both versions, so the extra time is in `structured: 'json'`. I have not profiled it. The 0.16.1 change that scans string values with their own line boundaries is my first guess, but that is only a guess.

## Expected

The per-call cost on short lines stays close to 0.16.0, or `docs/COVERAGE.md` gives the expected cost per call so callers can decide whether to sanitize on the main thread.

## Acceptance

- The rows above are within about 2x of 0.16.0, or the higher cost is documented.
- Detection results from 0.16.1 do not change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

## Summary

In the `documents` profile, some identifiers are only partly replaced: a word next to the number is redacted and the number itself stays. The output looks sanitized, and the number is still there. This is a leak.

## Reproduction (0.16.0)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
```

All values below are invented.

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `паспорт серия 4510 № 123456` | `паспорт [REDACTED] 4510 № 123456` |
| `Паспорт: серия 4510 номер 123456` | `Паспорт: [REDACTED] 4510 номер 123456` |
| `Passport series 4510 number 123456` | `Passport [REDACTED] 4510 number 123456` |
| `ОГРНИП 300000000000001` | `[REDACTED] 300000000000001` |
| `школа № 5` | `[REDACTED] 5` |

For comparison, the form without `серия` is handled correctly:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `паспорт 4510 123456` | `паспорт [REDACTED]` |
| `паспорт РФ 45 10 123456` | `паспорт [REDACTED] [REDACTED]` |

`серия` and `series` look like they are taken as the value of the passport label, so the span ends before the digits. I have not traced this.

## Expected

The identifying number is replaced, whatever words stand between the label and the number.

## Acceptance

- Each row of the first table has no digits of the number left in its output.
- Text without an identifier stays unchanged: `серия тестов 3 номер 5`, `Версия 1991`, `Уровень 3`.

title: documents profile: inconsistent redaction of url and time labels and 40-character hex values
body:
## Summary

In the `documents` profile, a few ordinary operational values are redacted depending only on the field label or on how the value is framed. They hold no personal data, and redacting them makes structured logs harder to read. Nothing leaks here, so this is lower priority than a miss.

## Reproduction (0.16.0)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';

const HASH = '9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a098765432';
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
const json = (v) =>
  sanitize(JSON.stringify(v), { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }).text;
```

### The `url` label

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `json({ url: '/api/v1/items' })` | `{"url":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `json({ path: '/api/v1/items' })` | `{"path":"/api/v1/items"}` |
| `text('url: /api/v1/items')` | `url: [REDACTED]` |

A relative path with no personal data is redacted only because of its label.

### The `time` label

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `json({ time: '2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z' })` | `{"time":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `json({ timestamp: '2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z' })` | `{"timestamp":"2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"}` |
| `text('time: 2026-01-15T10:30:00.000Z')` | `time: [REDACTED]` |

The same ISO timestamp is kept or redacted depending on the label, and `time` is a very common log field name.

### 40-character hex values

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `json({ commit: HASH })` | `{"commit":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `json({ note: HASH })` | `{"note":"[REDACTED]"}` |
| `json({ note: 'commit ' + HASH })` | `{"note":"commit 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a098765432"}` |
| `text(HASH)` | `9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a098765432` |

Redacting these may be deliberate, because some tokens are 40 hex characters. The inconsistency is the problem: the same value is treated as a secret in a JSON value and kept in text mode. If it can be a secret, the kept rows are leaks. If it cannot, the redacted rows are false positives.

## Expected

- A relative path under `url`, and an ISO timestamp under `time`, are kept.
- A 40-character hex value is handled the same way in text and structured modes.

## Acceptance

- The rows above follow one documented rule.
- A `url` value holding userinfo, a token or a personal path is still redacted.

title: structured json/jsonl: CV experience lines leak from single-line string values
body:
## Summary

In `structured: 'json'` and `structured: 'jsonl'` modes, the `documents` profile's CV experience-line rule does not fire on a single-line string value. The same text is redacted in text mode, and also when the JSON value has more than one line. This is a leak: the employer stays in the output.

## Reproduction (0.16.0)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';

const line = 'Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)';
const text = (s) => sanitize(s, { profile: 'documents' }).text;
const json = (v) =>
  sanitize(JSON.stringify(v), { profile: 'documents', structured: 'json' }).text;

text(line);
json({ note: line });
json({ list: [line] });
json({ payload: JSON.stringify({ note: line }) });
json({ note: `${line}\nвторая строка` });
json({ note: `первая строка\n${line}` });
```

| input | output | result |
|---|---|---|
| text mode | `Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021)` | redacted |
| `{ note: line }` | `{"note":"Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)"}` | **leak** |
| same, `structured: 'jsonl'` | `{"note":"Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)"}` | **leak** |
| `{ list: [line] }` | `{"list":["Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)"]}` | **leak** |
| JSON text inside a string value | `{"payload":"{\"note\":\"Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)\"}"}` | **leak** |
| line, then a second line | `{"note":"Менеджер, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021)\nвторая строка"}` | redacted |
| a first line, then the line | `{"note":"первая строка\nМенеджер, [REDACTED] (2019 – 2021)"}` | redacted |

## Possible cause

`structuredBatches` in `src/structured.js` scans each leaf as `"<key>": <raw token>`, so a single-line value does not start at a line start for the rules anchored with `^` (`experienceLine` and `experienceParenthesis` in `src/document-entities.js`). I have not traced why multi-line values do match, so this may be only part of the cause.

## Expected

A string value gets the same detection in structured modes as the same text in text mode, including rules anchored to a line start. Other anchored rules may be affected too; I only tested the experience-line rule.

## Workaround

Scanning each string value again in text mode catches the single-line cases, at the cost of a second pass per record. It does not catch the JSON-text-inside-a-string case.

## Acceptance

- All rows above are redacted in `json` and `jsonl` modes.
- Output stays parseable, and values without personal data stay byte-identical.

## Summary

Follow-up to #70. In 0.15.0 every row of #70 passes, but on the Russian CV corpus from #70 employer recall did not change. The experience-line rule only fires when the line starts with the job title. In the corpus, almost every experience line starts with a one-word label and a colon. My examples in #70 left that label out, sorry.

## Reproduction (0.15.0, Node 24)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const D = (t) => sanitize(t, { profile: 'documents',
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]', map: false } }).text;
```

| input | 0.15.0 output |
|---|---|
| `Менеджер по продажам, Северная торговая компания (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | `Менеджер по продажам, [ORGANIZATION_1] (…)` ✅ |
| `Опыт: Менеджер по продажам, Северная торговая компания (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Опыт: Менеджер по продажам, Ромашка (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Работа: Руководитель отдела продаж, Северный ветер (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `- Опыт: Менеджер, Ромашка (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Должность: Менеджер \| Опыт: Аналитик, Ромашка (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Опыт - Менеджер, Ромашка (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Менеджер, Ромашка (2018-01 – по н.в.)` | unchanged ❌ (`— н.в.` and `— по настоящее время` work) |
| `• Менеджер, Ромашка (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)` | `• Менеджер, [ORGANIZATION_1] (…)` ✅ |
| `Итог: Встреча, понедельник (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01) перенесена.` | unchanged ✅ (prose, must stay) |

## Measurements (aggregate, detection only, `profile: 'documents'`)

Employer mentions from the structured employer fields that are present in the text but not replaced:

| version | missed / present |
|---|---|
| 0.14.0 | 348 / 571 |
| 0.15.0 | 352 / 575 |

These are the same corpus and the same count method as #70. #70 counted unique values per document, so its numbers are smaller.

Of the missed employers that are directly followed by ` (YYYY-MM-DD — …)`, 384 of 412 (93%) sit on a line shaped `<Label>: <title>, <Employer> (<dates>)`. Here `<Label>` is one capitalised word, and the title is 1–9 words. Most of the rest have `|`, `.` or ` - ` before the title instead of `:`. The date range in the corpus is almost always `YYYY-MM-DD — YYYY-MM-DD`; a few end in `— по н.в.`.

## Expected

- The experience-line rule also accepts a short label prefix before the title. Treat a label of one or two words followed by `:`, ` - `, ` — ` or `|` the same as the start of a line or a list item. The date range stays the anchor, so prose with a comma and a date is still unaffected (the last row above).
- `по н.в.` is accepted as an end of the range, like `н.в.` and `по настоящее время`.
- Each row above produces `[ORGANIZATION_1]` for the employer, keeps the label and the title, and restores exactly. Default-profile fixtures do not change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Reused restore map: a bare lowercase part of a stored PERSON matches, merges another person and causes ERR_RESIDUAL
body:
## Summary

In 0.15.0 every fresh-map case from #67–#70 works; on a corpus of Russian CV texts, placeholder mode with a fresh map per document no longer refuses any document. With **one restore map reused across documents**, some documents are still refused with `ERR_RESIDUAL`. Every refusal has one cause: a single word that matches one part of a person stored in the reused map is replaced on its own. When it is lowercase, the next capitalised word is left in place and is then detected as a name next to the placeholder.

The documented contract (docs/API.md) says:

- "A part on its own does not: a bare `Данил` or `Сергеевич` is too ambiguous to imply from a longer value."
- "ambiguous surnames/initials and unrelated people are not intentionally merged."

For reused map entries, a bare surname part does match, in lower case too, and it merges a different person into the stored token.

## Reproduction (0.15.0, also 0.14.0, Node 24)

```js
import { sanitize, createRestoreMap } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const P = (map) => ({ profile: 'documents', transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map } });

const map = createRestoreMap();
sanitize('Кандидат: Петров Данил.', P(map)).text;              // 'Кандидат: Person-1.'

sanitize('Опыт: петров день, данил, мария.', P(map)).text;     // 'Опыт: Person-1 день, данил, мария.'
sanitize('Навыки: Битрикс петров, Excel.', P(map)).text;       // 'Навыки: Битрикс Person-1, Excel.'
sanitize('Навыки: Роман петров (CRM), отдел.', P(map)).text;   // 'Навыки: Роман Person-1 (CRM), отдел.'
sanitize('Опыт.\nСтек: Максим петрова (ПМ), отдел.', P(map));  // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
sanitize('Отзыв: Алина петрову, отдел.', P(map));              // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
```

With a fresh map, the same texts are returned unchanged (nothing is detected), and they do not throw.

Explicit `knownPersonal` follows the documented rule:

```js
sanitize('Сильный мороз. Мороз пришёл. Данил Мороз пришёл.', {
  knownOnly: true, knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value: 'Данил Мороз' }],
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' },
}).text; // 'Сильный мороз. Мороз пришёл. Person-1 пришёл.'
```

Whether a reused bare part matches depends on the word: `петров` matches, `мороз` does not.

## Problems

1. **A bare part of a reused PERSON entry matches.** The same rule should apply as for `knownPersonal`. `related()` in `src/placeholders.js` accepts a single-word candidate when it equals any part of a stored full alias (`parts.length === 1 && full.includes(parts[0])`).
2. **It matches lower case.** `петров день` in an unrelated sentence becomes `Person-1 день`. The lowercase word is ordinary text there, not a name.
3. **A different person is merged into the stored token.** In `Роман петров` the surname becomes `Person-1`, which is the token of `Петров Данил` from the previous document, and the given name `Роман` stays visible. A reader sees "Роман Person-1", the given name of one person attached to the token of another.
4. **The run fails.** For `Максим петрова` and `Алина петрову`, the leftover given name next to the placeholder is detected as `PERSON/name-identity`, and the run throws `ERR_RESIDUAL`. Failing closed is right, but the cause is the bare-part match, not the input.

## Measurements (aggregate, `profile: 'documents'`, placeholder mode)

175 unique Russian CV texts, processed in order:

| version | fresh map per document: refused | one shared map: refused |
|---|---|---|
| 0.14.0 | 2 | 16 |
| 0.15.0 | 0 | 14 |

In 0.15.0 all 14 shared-map refusals are `ERR_RESIDUAL` from the final residual check. In each, the leftover finding is `PERSON/name-identity` on `<Capitalised word> Person-N`, where `Person-N` is an entry from an earlier document. In the cases checked, the leftover word is not the name of the person whose document it is.

## Expected

- A reused map PERSON entry matches the same forms as an explicit `knownPersonal` value: the full value and its contiguous parts together, all cases, both orders, initials. A bare single part does not match on its own, unless it was stored as its own value.
- A match is never in lower case when the stored value is capitalised, unless the whole value appears in lower case (`петров данил`).
- If a bare part ever does match (for example as an opt-in), the span covers the adjacent given name or patronymic of the same mention. The adjacent name is not left next to the placeholder, and a mention with a different given name gets its own token.
- The shared-map refusals above disappear without new under-redaction. The `#67`–`#70` examples keep working.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: documents profile: employers in CV experience lines ('<title>, <Employer> (YYYY-MM – YYYY-MM)') are missed — 65% of employers on a Russian CV corpus
body:
## Summary

The `documents` profile now passes every row of #59. On real Russian CV text, though, most employer names are still not detected. That is because the most common way a CV names an employer is an experience line, `<job title>, <Employer> (<dates>)`, which has no legal form, no quotes and no context word.

Measured on 236 Russian CV texts against the employer names in their own structured fields (detection only, no `knownPersonal`; aggregate counts):

| entity | present in text | not replaced |
|---|---|---|
| ORGANIZATION | 303 | 196 (65%) |
| EDUCATION | 15 | 14 |
| PERSON | 166 | 10 |
| LOCATION | 59 | 4 |

The context before and after each missed employer, reduced to its shape (letters → `x`, digits → `9`):

| count | shape |
|---|---|
| 114 | `x x, ‹Employer› (9999-99-` |
| 13 | `x, ‹Employer› (9999-99-` |
| 11 | ` x, ‹Employer› (9999-99-` |
| ~40 | other `<title>, ‹Employer› (9999-99-` variants |

So about 90% of the misses are the experience-line pattern.

## Reproduction (0.14.0)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const D = (t) => sanitize(t, { profile: 'documents',
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]', map: false } }).text;
```

| input | output | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `Менеджер по продажам, Северная торговая компания (2019-05 – 2021-03)` | unchanged | `Менеджер по продажам, [ORGANIZATION_1] (2019-05 – 2021-03)` |
| `Ведущий инженер, Ромашка (2018-01 – 2020-12)` | unchanged | `Ведущий инженер, [ORGANIZATION_1] (…)` |
| `QA engineer, Acme Solutions (2020-02 – 2023-06)` | unchanged | `QA engineer, [ORGANIZATION_1] (…)` |
| `Аналитик, «Северный ветер» (2018-01 – 2020-12)` | unchanged | quoted name without a legal form |
| `Менеджер, Северная торговая компания (май 2019 — март 2021)` | unchanged | month-name date range |
| `Менеджер по продажам — Северная торговая компания, 2019–2021` | unchanged | dash separator, year range |
| `Менеджер (Северная торговая компания), 2019–2021` | unchanged | employer in parentheses |
| `Руководитель отдела, ООО Ромашка (2018-01 – 2020-12)` | `Руководитель отдела, [ORGANIZATION_1] (…)` | ok (legal form) |

## Proposal

Keep it inside the opt-in `documents` profile, at a lower confidence:

- **Experience line.** At the start of a line or list item, the span between a short leading phrase and a following date range is an ORGANIZATION. The date range is `(YYYY-MM – YYYY-MM)`, `(YYYY – YYYY)`, `(<month> YYYY — <month> YYYY|по настоящее время|н.в.)`, or `, YYYY–YYYY`. The leading phrase is up to N words, mostly lowercase after the first. The separator is `, `, ` — ` or parentheses. The date range is the anchor, so ordinary prose with a comma is not affected.
- **Quoted names.** A quoted name (`«…»`, `"…"`) directly in an employer slot is an ORGANIZATION even without a legal form.
- **Propagation.** As with #59, propagate each employer found this way to its other mentions in the same document.

## Acceptance

- Each row above produces the expected output under `profile: 'documents'`, and restores exactly.
- Default-profile fixtures do not change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: ERR_RESIDUAL in placeholder mode: '@handle/email' leaves '@Email-1', and 'Name-99' organizations leave digits glued to the placeholder
body:
## Summary

In 0.14.0, placeholder mode now succeeds on almost every document that 0.13.0 refused with `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION`. Thank you. On a corpus of 236 Russian CV texts, however, 12 documents (5%) are still refused, now with `ERR_RESIDUAL`. Both causes below are cases where a finding's span stops one character short and the leftover character, glued to the placeholder, is detected again.

## 1. Messenger handle followed by an email: `@` stays before `Email-1`

```js
import { sanitize, createRestoreMap } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const ph = () => ({ transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: createRestoreMap() } });

sanitize('Telegram: @Janedoe2024/jane_doe@example.com', ph());     // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
sanitize('Telegram/Email: @JaneDoe/jane@example.com', ph());       // throws ERR_RESIDUAL
sanitize('Telegram: @Janedoe2024/jane_doe@example.com').text;      // 'Telegram: @[REDACTED]'
sanitize('tg: @jane_doe / jane_doe@example.com', ph()).text;       // 'tg: Username-1 / Email-1'  ok
```

`inspect` reports a single `EMAIL/email` finding `Janedoe2024/jane_doe@example.com`: the local part starts after the leading `@` and includes the `/`. The output becomes `@Email-1`, which `messenger-handle` detects as a new username, so the residual check fails closed. In the default mode the output is `@[REDACTED]`, which keeps the shape of a handle.

Expected: `@handle/email` (a common "Telegram/Email: …" CV line) yields a username and an email (`Username-1/Email-1`), or one finding that includes the leading `@`. In either case the output contains no residual.

## 2. `Name-NN` organizations: span stops before the digits

```js
const P = (map) => ({ profile: 'documents', transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map } });

sanitize('Опыт в компании Вектор-99, отдел продаж', P(createRestoreMap())).text;
// 'Опыт в компании Organization-199, отдел продаж'

sanitize('в компании Вектор-99 и в компании Гранит-7, позже в компании Вектор-99', P(createRestoreMap())).text;
// 'в компании Organization-199 и в компании Organization-27, позже в компании Organization-199'
```

`organization-context` finds `Вектор-` (with the hyphen, without the digits). The placeholder replaces that span, and the digits remain glued to it, so `Organization-1` + `99` reads as `Organization-199`:

- The text now shows a placeholder number that does not exist. A reader or a downstream model sees "entity 199" (or 1399 with a reused map), not entity 1 followed by "-99". `restore` still returns the exact input, so the restore map itself is fine.
- With a reused map, `Вектор` and `Вектор-` become two different entities (`Organization-1`, then `Organization-2` + `99` = `Organization-299`).
- A later mention in the same sentence is missed: `Работал в компании Вектор-1, затем Вектор-2.` → `… Organization-131, затем Вектор-2.`
- On the corpus, with one restore map shared across documents (as needed for consistent entity numbers), a residual `organization-context` finding on the placeholder text (`Organization-` before digits) makes the document fail with `ERR_RESIDUAL`.

Expected: the organization span includes the `-<digits>` suffix (`Вектор-99`, `Гранит-7`, `Альфа-1`), the same as quoted names with digits (fixed in #59: `АО «Гранит-2»`). No placeholder is ever directly followed by a digit; if a span must end there, the placeholder is delimited, or the run fails. Later mentions of the same name are replaced too.

## Measurements (0.14.0, `profile: 'documents'`, placeholder mode, aggregate only)

| restore map | documents | refused |
|---|---|---|
| fresh per document | 236 | 2 (`ERR_RESIDUAL`, cause 1) |
| one shared map | 236 | 12 (`ERR_RESIDUAL`, causes 1 and 2) |

0.13.0 refused 118 of the same documents with `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION` (#58).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: knownPersonal: masculine instrumental patronymic (-ичем), reversed name order and surname+given of a three-part value are still missed
body:
## Summary

In 0.14.0, `knownPersonal` matches many Russian case forms, which is a big improvement. But some forms of a known full name still pass through unchanged, even with `knownOnly: true`. The value the caller explicitly listed then stays in the output.

## Reproduction (0.14.0)

```js
import { sanitize } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const t = (value, text) => sanitize(text, {
  knownOnly: true,
  knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value }],
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' },
}).text;
```

| known value | input | output |
|---|---|---|
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `о Петрове Даниле Сергеевиче.` | `о Person-1.` ✅ |
| `Смирнова Алина Игоревна` | `со Смирновой Алиной Игоревной` | `со Person-1` ✅ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `с Петровым Данилом Сергеевичем.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Данил Сергеевич` | `с Данилом Сергеевичем.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Сергеевич` | `с Сергеевичем.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `Данил Сергеевич Петров пришёл; Данилу Сергеевичу Петрову.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `с Петровым Данилом.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил` | `с Петровым Данилом.` | `с Person-1.` ✅ |

## Gaps

1. **Instrumental case of masculine patronymics** (`-ович/-евич` → `-овичем/-евичем`) is not generated, so every masculine full name in the instrumental case is missed. Feminine (`-овной`) works.
2. **Word order.** `Фамилия Имя Отчество` and `Имя Отчество Фамилия` are the two everyday Russian orders. A known value in one order does not match the other, in any case.
3. **Partial forms of a three-part value.** `Фамилия Имя` (without the patronymic) is not matched when the known value has three parts, although the same pair matches when it is listed on its own.

## Expected

- A known Russian full name matches in all six cases.
- It matches in both name orders.
- It matches as surname + given name without the patronymic, all mapped to the same entity (the same `Person-N` and the same fake identity).

The caller can list every variant by hand, but then the bounded case matching gives no benefit for full names.

## Notes

- With `со` before a placeholder, the output reads `со Person-1`. This is cosmetic and probably fine to keep.
- Environment: 0.14.0, Node 20.

comments.body:
Further forms that are missed in 0.14.0 (`knownOnly: true`, `knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value }]`, placeholder mode):

| known value | input | output |
|---|---|---|
| `Семёнов Пётр` | `Семенов Петр пришёл.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Семенов Петр` | `Семёнов Пётр пришёл.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `Петров Д. С. подписал.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `Петров Д.С. подписал.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `Д. С. Петров подписал.` | unchanged ❌ |
| `Петров Данил Сергеевич` | `ПЕТРОВ ДАНИЛ СЕРГЕЕВИЧ` | `Person-1` ✅ |

- **ё/е.** Russian text writes `ё` as `е` most of the time, and the two spellings of one name are the same name. Matching should treat `ё` and `е` (and `Ё`/`Е`) as equal in both directions, while restore keeps the original surface.
- **Initials.** `Фамилия И. О.`, `Фамилия И.О.` and `И. О. Фамилия` are the standard short forms of a full name in Russian documents: signatures, orders, letters. A known three-part value could cover these forms of the same entity, in the same cases as the surname.
- **Parts of a full name.** The surname alone (`Петров подписал.`) or the given name alone is not matched from a full-name entry; it is matched only when listed separately. If this is intended, a sentence in the `knownPersonal` docs would help ("list each part you want matched on its own").

acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: knownPersonal matches inside words: 'Lee' in 'Sleep' → 'S[PERSON_1]p', 'Смирнов' → '[PERSON_1]ка'
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` values match **inside** longer words, case-insensitively, with no word boundary. Placeholder output then cuts words apart.

v0.13.0 (ee7b51c), `sanitize(text, { knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value }], transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]', map: false } })`:

| known value | text | known-personal findings | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Павлов` | `Отчество: Сергей Павлович.` | `Павлов` | `Отчество: [PERSON_1].` |
| `Арсенова` | `Автор: Сарсенова Анна.` | `арсенова` | `Автор: [PERSON_1].` |
| `Смирнов` | `Город: Смирновка.` | `Смирнов` | `Город: [PERSON_1]ка.` |
| `Lee` | `Sleep well, Lee.` | `lee`, `Lee` | `S[PERSON_1]p well, [PERSON_1].` |
| `Ann` | `Annual report by Ann.` | `Ann`, `Ann` | `[PERSON_1]ual report by [PERSON_1].` |

- `Lee` inside `Sleep` and `Ann` inside `Annual` show that any short known name corrupts ordinary words.
- `Арсенова` inside `Сарсенова` (a different surname) matches mid-word, lowercase.
- `Смирнов` → `[PERSON_1]ка` and `Павлов` inside the patronymic `Павлович` show a prefix match that cuts the word.

This also makes known-value scans noisy: a verification pass reports "known value still present" for text that holds only other words.

## Expected

- A known value matches only at word boundaries (Unicode letters and digits on both sides count as word characters), so `Lee` does not match in `Sleep` and `Арсенова` does not match in `Сарсенова`.
- When a known value is found as a prefix of a longer word, the whole word is replaced, never `[PERSON_1]ка`. Inflected forms are a separate request (#60), and they should be matched as whole words too.
- Case-insensitive matching is fine, but not across a lowercase→uppercase word start (`арсенова` in `Сарсенова`).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Replace only knownPersonal values with a restore map (known scores 0.85 < detections 0.9; redact() returns no map)
body:
## Problem

There is no way to replace **only** the caller's known values while keeping a restore map.

Use case: a document contains a few real people (known list) and also deliberately fictional example names, sample phones and company names that must stay as they are. The goal is to replace exactly the known values, reversibly.

v0.13.0 (ee7b51c), text:

```
Отчёт подготовил Петров Данил Сергеевич. Пример в документации: Иванов Иван Иванович, тел. +7 900 000-00-00, ООО «Ромашка», г. Казань.
```

`knownPersonal: [{ type: 'PERSON', value: 'Петров Данил Сергеевич' }]`, `profile: 'documents'`:

`inspect()` findings:

```
PERSON 0.85 "Петров Данил Сергеевич" known-personal
PERSON 0.9  "Петров Данил Сергеевич" name-identity
PERSON 0.9  "Иванов Иван Иванович"   name-identity
PERSON 0.7  "Иван Иванович"          name-gazetteer
PHONE  0.85 "+7 900 000-00-00"       international-phone
ORGANIZATION 0.7 "ООО «Ромашка»"     organization-legal-form
LOCATION 0.75 "Казань."              location-label
```

What the existing options give:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `minConfidence: 0.85` | `[PERSON_1] … [PERSON_2], тел. [PHONE_1]` (example name and phone replaced) |
| `minConfidence: 0.9` | `[PERSON_1] … [PERSON_2]` (example name replaced) |
| `minConfidence: 1` | nothing replaced, known value included |
| `inspect()` → keep `rule === 'known-personal'` → `redact(text, findings, { transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' } })` | `Отчёт подготовил [PERSON_1]. … Иванов Иван Иванович …` as a plain **string**: correct text, but **no restore map** |

So known values score below ordinary detections (0.85 vs 0.9), and the one path that isolates them (`redact`) drops the map.

## Expected

Any of:

1. An option such as `detection: 'known'` / `knownOnly: true` for `sanitize()` that turns off automatic personal detection and replaces only `knownPersonal` (and `knownSecrets`) values; credentials could still be protected unless `credentialsOnly`-style filtering is asked for.
2. `redact()` with `transformation: { mode: 'placeholder' }` returning `{ text, map }` like `sanitize()`, so callers can supply their own findings and still restore.
3. Known values scored at confidence 1.0, so `minConfidence: 1` keeps only them (simplest, but mixes two meanings into one threshold).

The same applies to `mode: 'fake'`: a known-only run should not rewrite fictional example names.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: fake mode: Russian given names (Данил, Максим, Алина) become surnames, and one given name can stay unchanged
body:
## Problem

In `transformation: { mode: 'fake' }`, Russian names are rewritten part by part, but several common given names are classified as surnames. The fake then has two surnames, which reads as a broken name and changes the name's shape:

Input: `Автор: <name>.`, key `example-key-0123456789abcdef`, v0.13.0 (ee7b51c).

| Input | fake, detection only | fake, with `knownPersonal: [{type:'PERSON', value:<name>}]` |
|---|---|---|
| Петров Данил Сергеевич | Баранов Муравьев Филимонович | Баранов Муравьев Филимонович |
| Данил Сергеевич Петров | Данил Филимонович Баранов | Муравьев Филимонович Баранов |
| Петров Данил | Баранов Муравьев | Баранов Муравьев |
| Данил Петров | Муравьев Баранов | Муравьев Баранов |
| Кузнецов Максим Антонович | Колесников Рожков Гавриилович | Колесников Рожков Гавриилович |
| Максим Кузнецов | Рожков Колесников | Рожков Колесников |
| Смирнова Алина | Потапова Мамонтова | Потапова Мамонтова |
| Алина Смирнова | Мамонтова Потапова | Мамонтова Потапова |
| Соколова Мария Ивановна | Данилова Элеонора Харитоновна | Данилова Элеонора Харитоновна |

Observations:

1. `Данил`, `Максим`, `Алина` get surname fakes in every word order; `Мария` is handled correctly. The patronymic is enough context to know the middle token is a given name, but it is still faked as a surname.
2. Row 2, detection only: the given name `Данил` is left **unchanged** while the rest is faked, so part of the real name stays in the output. With `knownPersonal` it is replaced (but as a surname).
3. Gender agreement of surname and patronymic is right; only the role of the given-name token is wrong.

## Expected

- In `Surname Given [Patronymic]` and `Given [Patronymic] Surname` forms, the given-name slot gets a given-name fake of the same gender (`Петров Данил Сергеевич` → e.g. `Баранов Игорь Филимонович`).
- A token inside a detected person span is never left as is (row 2).
- When the role of a token is unknown, the whole span is replaced with a complete fake name of the same shape instead of a per-token guess.

A deterministic way to decide the slot: a token followed by a patronymic (`-ович/-евич/-ична/-овна/-евна`) is a given name; with two tokens, the one that matches surname morphology (`-ов/-ев/-ин/-ский/-ова/-ева/-ина/-ская`) is the surname. A larger given-name list would also fix these specific names.

## Use case

Replacing real names in test fixtures and example data with consistent, natural-looking fakes so the text keeps reading like the original (one surname, one given name, gender kept).
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: knownPersonal and map entries: match inflected and partial forms of the same entity
body:
## Problem

`knownPersonal` is the best tool when the caller already knows the private values (for example from the structured fields of the same record). With it, every exact mention is replaced. But in Russian (and other inflected languages) the same entity mostly appears in other case forms, and those stay in the output:

```js
const knownPersonal = [
  { type: 'LOCATION', value: 'Кострома' },
  { type: 'ORGANIZATION', value: 'Ромашка' },
  { type: 'PERSON', value: 'Анна Смирнова' },
];
const opts = { profile: 'documents', knownPersonal,
  transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: createRestoreMap({ format: '[{TYPE}_{n}]' }) } };

sanitize('Кострома; ООО «Ромашка»', opts).text;              // "[LOCATION_1]; [ORGANIZATION_1]"  ok
sanitize('Живу в Костроме, работал в Ромашке.', opts).text;  // unchanged
sanitize('Отзыв от Анны Смирновой', opts).text;              // unchanged
sanitize('Смирновой Анне', opts).text;                       // unchanged
```

Person linking already handles masculine `-ов/-ев` surnames (`Ивановым`), but not feminine `-ова/-ева` (`Смирновой`), given names (`Анны`, `Анне`), or the case forms of organizations and places (`Костроме`, `Ромашке`). In model-written summaries about a document, inflected mentions are the norm, so a sanitized summary still names the person, the employer and the city.

A related gap: a known multi-word organization (`ООО «Северная торговая компания»`) is often mentioned later by its distinctive part only (`Северная торговая компания`, `в Северной торговой компании`).

## Proposal

- For `knownPersonal` and for entities already in the restore map, also match bounded inflected forms per locale. For Russian: noun/adjective case endings for the last letters of each word (`-а/-ы/-е/-у/-ой/-ою`, `-ий/-ого/-ому/-им/-ом`, `-ь/-я/-ю/-ем/-и`, feminine surnames `-ова/-ой`, `-ая/-ой/-ую`), with a minimum stem length so short words do not over-match.
- Match the distinctive part of a known organization (without the legal form and quotes), including its inflected forms.
- Each matched surface is stored as a separate original surface of the same entry, so exact restore keeps working, as it already does for `Ивановым`.
- Optional, for structured input: `personalFields: { 'company': 'ORGANIZATION', 'first_name': 'PERSON', … }` to take known values from fields of the same JSON record and apply them to all its other strings, so callers do not have to collect them manually.

## Acceptance

- All four examples above produce placeholders for every mention, and `restore` returns the exact input.
- No new replacements on existing fixtures that do not use `knownPersonal`.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: documents profile: Russian employer, school and city forms that are still missed
body:
## Problem

The `documents` profile (thanks for #55) catches `ООО Ромашка`, `ООО "Север Плюс"` and `ООО ТЕХНОСОФТ`. On Russian CVs, though, most employers, schools and cities still come through. Measured on a corpus of Russian-language CVs against their own structured fields (employer/school/city lists), detection alone missed about 68% of employer mentions, 16 of 17 school mentions and about half of the city mentions. Synthetic reproductions with `profile: 'documents'` and placeholder mode:

| Input | Output today | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `ООО «Северная торговая компания» — менеджер` | unchanged | `[ORGANIZATION_1] — менеджер` (lowercase words inside the quoted name) |
| `АО «Гранит-2» — инженер` | unchanged | digits and hyphens inside the quoted name |
| `Работал в ООО «Ромашка» и затем в Ромашка.` | `[ORGANIZATION_1] … в Ромашка.` | the bare name of an already detected organization is the same entity |
| `Ромашка Групп, ведущий инженер` | unchanged | `Групп`/`Group`/`Холдинг`/`Holding` as organization markers |
| `Московский государственный университет, 2015` | unchanged | adjective + lowercase words + institution type word |
| `Северный федеральный университет имени Ломоносова` | unchanged | `имени <Name>` tail is part of the name |
| `Санкт-Петербургский политехнический университет` | unchanged | hyphenated adjectival city prefix |
| `НИУ ВШЭ, магистратура` | unchanged | institution acronyms after type acronyms (`НИУ`, `МГУ`-style uppercase acronyms in an education context) |
| `Город: Кострома` | unchanged | location label followed by a colon |
| `Проживаю: Кострома` / `Кострома, готов к переезду` | unchanged | common residence phrasing |
| `Ярославль, Россия` | unchanged | `<City>, <Country>` pattern; also a larger city list (a regional city of ~600k people is missing) |
| `Меня зовут Анна, я тестировщик.` / `С уважением, Анна` | unchanged | a single given name after a self-introduction or a sign-off (`С уважением, Анна Смирнова` already works) |

## Proposal

- In quoted names after a legal form, accept the whole quoted span (any words, digits, hyphens, up to a bound) instead of capitalized words only.
- Propagate a detected organization's core name (the quoted part / the part without the legal form) to its other mentions in the same document or stream.
- Russian education names: an optional adjectival prefix (`…ский`, `…ный`, `…вый`, hyphenated forms), lowercase words up to the institution type word, an optional `имени …` tail; uppercase acronyms in an education context.
- Location labels with `:` and residence phrases; a `<City>, <Country>` pattern; a larger bounded offline vocabulary, e.g. GeoNames `cities15000` subset per locale (already mentioned in the #56 case study).
- Given name alone after self-introduction / sign-off phrases, using the existing name gazetteer.

All of this can stay inside the opt-in `documents` profile with lower confidence, as now.

## Acceptance

Each row above produces the expected output under `profile: 'documents'`, with fixtures, and the existing default-profile fixtures do not change.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Placeholder mode refuses ordinary text containing GPT-4, ISO-9001, Windows-10 (ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION)
body:
## Problem

With the default placeholder format `{Type}-{n}`, `sanitize` throws `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION` for any text containing an ordinary `Letters-Number` token, even when that token has nothing to do with the placeholder labels:

```js
import { sanitize, createRestoreMap } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const t = { transformation: { mode: 'placeholder', map: createRestoreMap() } };
sanitize('Jane Doe knows GPT-4.', t);          // throws ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION
sanitize('Jane Doe, ISO-9001 audits', t);      // throws
sanitize('Jane Doe uses Windows-10', t);       // throws
sanitize('Jane Doe uses Python 3', t);         // ok -> "Person-1 uses Python 3"
```

The namespace check in `src/placeholders.js` (`preparePlaceholderText`) turns `{Type}` into `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and `{n}` into `[1-9][0-9]*`, without word boundaries. So `GPT-4`, `ISO-9001`, `COVID-19`, `Web-3`, `SQL-92`, `S-300` and even `abc-1` inside a longer word all count as collisions.

On a corpus of technical CVs (version numbers, standards, product names), every single document was refused with the default format. Switching to `[{TYPE}_{n}]` avoided it, but the default should work on normal prose.

## Expected

- Reserve only labels the sanitizer can actually emit (`Person`, `Organization`, `Education`, `Location`, `Email`, `Phone`, `Date`, `Credential` and the other detector type labels, in the casing the template uses), not every identifier.
- Match with token boundaries, so `xPerson-1y` and `Person-1a` are not collisions, while a standalone `Person-1` still is.
- When a map is reused, an existing token of that map in the input is still a collision (as today).

## Acceptance

- The four examples above succeed with the default format; `GPT-4`, `ISO-9001` and `Windows-10` stay unchanged in the output and restore exactly.
- `sanitize('Person-1 met Jane Doe', ...)` still throws `ERR_PLACEHOLDER_COLLISION`.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Detect organizations, schools and locations without a preceding context word
body:
## Problem

Organizations are only detected after a context word. The rule in `src/personal.js` matches a capitalized word directly after `компании|организации|company|organization|société|empresa|Firma`. Typical documents name employers, schools and places without such a word, so they stay in the output:

```
2019–2023  Acme Ltd, Senior Engineer
2015–2019  Northfield State University
Based in Springfield, relocated from Riverton
```

None of `Acme Ltd`, `Northfield State University`, `Springfield` or `Riverton` is a finding today, as far as I can tell from the rules. The same holds for other languages, e.g. `ООО «Ромашка»`, `Ромашка GmbH`.

Together with names, these quasi-identifiers (employer + school + city + years) are often enough to re-identify a person. That makes "the output is anonymous" claims weak for CVs, profiles and similar documents even when every name and email is removed.

## Proposal

- **Organizations by legal form**, with or without quotes and in either order, e.g. `Inc`, `LLC`, `Ltd`, `GmbH`, `AG`, `S.A.`, `ООО`, `АО`, `ПАО`, `ИП`, plus the other locales of the gazetteer.
- **Educational institutions** by type words (`University`, `College`, `Institute`, `Университет`, `Институт`…) next to a proper name.
- **Locations** (cities, regions) from a bounded gazetteer and after location labels (`based in`, `located in`, `г.`, `город`).
- **New types**, so placeholder/fake modes can number them: `ORGANIZATION`, `EDUCATION` (or `ORGANIZATION` with a subtype) and `LOCATION`.
- **Public exemptions** keep working through the existing `publicEntities` list, for organizations that are fine to keep, and through `knownPersonal` for ones that must always go.
- **Confidence.** These findings are lower-confidence than identifiers. Expose a confidence and a profile switch, so log sanitization does not suddenly redact every capitalized company name in stack traces.

## Acceptance

- Fixtures for each supported locale with employers, schools and cities in list form (no context words) are detected.
- No new findings on the existing credential/log fixtures under the default profile.
- `COVERAGE.md` lists the new types and their limits.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Reversible typed placeholders (Person-1, Organization-1) with a private restore map (JSON / Links Notation) and a no-map full anonymization mode
body:
## Problem

None of the current transformations gives readable, consistent placeholders that can be reversed by the data owner:

| Mode | Output for `Jane Doe` | Same person twice → same token | Readable | Reversible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redact` | `[REDACTED]` | no (every person is the same token) | yes | no |
| `pseudonym` | `[PSEUDONYM_3f9a…]` (24 hex chars, `src/transforms.js`) | yes | no | no (HMAC) |
| `format-preserving` | shape pseudonym | yes | no | no (documented as non-reversible) |
| `fake` | realistic fake name | yes | yes, but looks real | no |

A common use case needs something else: turn real documents (CVs, emails, chat transcripts, LLM request/response logs) into samples that can be shared, committed as test fixtures or sent to a model, where

- each entity becomes a typed, numbered placeholder: `Person-1`, `Person-2`, `Organization-1`, `Email-1`, `Phone-1`, `Location-1`, `Date-1`…;
- the same entity gets the same placeholder everywhere (across fields, records and files), so relations stay visible ("Person-1 worked at Organization-1 with Person-2");
- the owner can restore the original data later from a private map, and nobody else can.

## Proposal

1. **`placeholder` transformation**: `{mode: 'placeholder'}` replaces each personal finding with `<Type>-<n>`. Numbering is per type, in order of first appearance. Format configurable (`Person-1`, `[PERSON_1]`, `{{person_1}}`), with a check that the chosen format cannot collide with text already in the input.
2. **Private restore map**: the operation can return or write a map from placeholder to original value(s). Two serializations:
   - JSON;
   - [Links Notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation), e.g. `(Person-1: "Jane Doe")`.

   The map file is written with mode `0600`, never into the sanitized output, and is refused as an input to publication checks.
3. **Reuse a map**: passing an existing map continues it, so a corpus processed in several runs or files keeps `Person-1` meaning the same person, and new entities get the next free numbers.
4. **Restore**: `restore(text, map)` and `sensitive-data-sanitizer restore safe.txt --map map.lino`. It also works on text derived from the sanitized output, e.g. a model answer that quotes `Person-1`, which is the main reason to keep the map.
5. **Full anonymization**: the same mode with no map kept (`map: false`). The output is then irreversible: the numbering lives only in memory and is discarded, and residual verification runs as for `redact`.

## Details to decide

- **Variants of one entity.** `Jane Doe`, `J. Doe`, `Doe`, transliterations and inflected forms (Russian `Ивановым` / `Иванова`) should map to one placeholder. The existing component-identity logic of `fake` already links some of these. The map has to keep each original surface form so that restore gives back the exact original text, not a normalized one.
- **Structured input.** JSON/JSONL values and keys get the same placeholders as free text; the output must stay valid JSON.
- **Credentials.** Keep them fully redacted by default and never put them into the map unless explicitly requested.
- **Safety of the map.** Document clearly that the map is the personal data. The output alone is safe only to the extent detection is complete (see the coverage limits in the README).

## Acceptance

- Round trip: `restore(sanitize(text, {mode: 'placeholder'}).text, map) === text` for free text, JSON and JSONL fixtures, including inflected and transliterated names.
- Same entity in two files processed with one reused map gets the same placeholder.
- With `map: false`, no map is produced anywhere and the output passes residual verification.
- Both map formats parse back to the same map.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required
