title: Detect dates of birth in natural language and loose labels
body:
## Summary

Dates of birth are detected only with a structured key such as `dob: ...`. Natural-language and loosely labelled birth dates pass through. A real leak included remarks like "real DOB `02/03/1990`".

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'she was born on 07/12/1985 in Kazan',
  'All correct - real DOB `02/03/1990`',
  'birth date 1985-12-07',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted. 'Дата рождения: 07.12.1985' is detected, so the gap is label coverage, not date parsing.
```

## Expected

- `DATE_OF_BIRTH` when birth vocabulary (born, birth date, DOB, дата рождения, д.р., родился/родилась, Geburtsdatum, fecha de nacimiento, date de naissance) appears within a short window before a date, including markdown/backtick quoting.
- All common date shapes: `dd/mm/yyyy`, `mm/dd/yyyy`, `dd.mm.yyyy`, ISO, and month names in English and Russian.
- Keep plain dates (commit dates, timestamps) untouched without birth context.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Detect travel booking data: PNR/booking references, e-ticket and visa numbers
body:
## Summary

Travel booking data is not detected: airline booking references (PNR / record locator), e-ticket numbers and visa or e-visa application numbers. In a real leak, a booking reference and airline notification identifiers were published from sanitized sessions.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'booking reference K7QWZP',
  'PNR: XKJHQZ, record locator XKJHQZ',
  'код брони K7QWZP',
  'e-ticket 098-2401234567',
  'e-visa registration code E260512ABCDEF',
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted.
```

## Expected

- `BOOKING_REFERENCE`: 5–8 alphanumeric characters after context words (booking reference/code, reservation code, confirmation code, record locator, PNR, код брони, номер брони, бронирование).
- `TICKET_NUMBER`: 13-digit IATA e-ticket numbers (3-digit airline prefix + 10 digits) with context.
- `VISA_NUMBER`: visa / e-visa / registration numbers after context words.
- Personal category, so masking transformations apply.

## Tests

Negatives must include ordinary uppercase words after "booking" (for example `booking reference: NONE`) and git short SHAs.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Detect passport numbers without explicit labels (Russian domestic/international and country formats)
body:
## Summary

Passport numbers are only detected when they follow an explicit label such as `паспорт:`. Formats commonly found in logs and AI sessions without such a label are missed. This contributed to a real leak of passport data.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
const s = createSanitizer();
for (const t of [
  'series and number: 45 17 839204',          // RU domestic passport
  '4517 839204',                              // RU domestic, compact
  'загран 75 4930281',                        // RU international passport
]) console.log((await s.sanitize(t)).text);
// None are redacted. (By contrast, 'UK passport 123456789' and 'pasaporte AB1234567' are detected.)
```

## Expected

- Russian domestic passport `dd dd dddddd` / `dddd dddddd` and international `dd ddddddd` as format rules, with higher confidence when Russian/English passport vocabulary appears within a window (not only as a `key: value` label).
- Country formats with validation where public algorithms exist (ICAO 9-character document numbers with check digit, US 9 digits, UK 9 digits, DE `[CFGHJK][0-9CFGHJKLMNPRTVWXYZ]{8}`, IN `[A-Z][0-9]{7}`, KR `M[0-9]{3}[A-Z][0-9]{4}`, IT `[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{7}`), using a Presidio-style confidence model: low score without context, high with context or checksum.
- Multilingual context vocabulary: passport, паспорт, загранпаспорт, серия, номер, pasaporte, Reisepass, passeport, passaporto, 护照, パスポート.

## Tests

Positive and negative fixtures per country, including numbers next to unrelated digits (timestamps, version numbers, phone numbers) to keep false positives measured.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Detect passport machine-readable zones (ICAO 9303 MRZ): real passport data leaked
body:
## Summary

Passport machine-readable zones (ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ) are not detected at all. In a real publication of sanitized AI coding sessions, several MRZ lines of real passports passed through `createSanitizer().sanitize()` unchanged and became public. The data was contained, but passport data is critical personal data and must never pass.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
import { createSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const s = createSanitizer();
console.log((await s.sanitize(
  'mrz: P<RUSKOVALEVA<<MARINA<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<\n5839204716RUS8204117M310519<<<<<<<<<<<<<<02'
)).text);
// Both lines are returned unchanged, even with the "mrz:" label.
```

## Expected

Detect all ICAO 9303 MRZ formats regardless of context:

- TD3 (passports, 2 x 44 characters), TD2 (2 x 36), TD1 (ID cards, 3 x 30), MRV-A/MRV-B visas.
- The name line (`P<`, `I<`, `A<`, `C<`, `V<` + issuing state + names with `<` fillers).
- The data line, also when only a fragment is present (document number + check digit + nationality + birth date + check digit + sex + expiry + check digit). Real logs often contain a truncated or reflowed line.
- Validate check digits (7-3-1 weights) to raise confidence, but do NOT require valid check digits to redact: a typo in a real MRZ is still personal data.
- New types such as `PASSPORT_MRZ`, category `personal`.

## Tests

- Positive: synthetic TD1/TD2/TD3 lines with valid and invalid check digits; line fragments; MRZ embedded in JSON strings with `\n` escapes; lowercase-free OCR variants with spaces between groups.
- Negative: long runs of `<` alone, base64 strings, C++ templates like `vector<<int>>`.
- Residual verification must fail if an MRZ survives.

Competitors: no open tool has a complete MRZ detector (Presidio only touches TD1 inside the German ID recognizer), so this would be a real differentiator.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required

title: Collect all best practices we used to do sanitation of sensitive data from our projects
body:
Check our all our organizations repositories:
- link-foundation
- linksplatform
- link-assistant
- konard (user)

For example:
- github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind
- github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai
- github.com/konard/documents-processing

Collect all logic and best practices we used for sanitation, and make sure we implement the most robust framework/library and cli on a the market to fully sanitize any text files like logs, AI sessions and so on.

We should be able to do sanitation of personal data (names, emails and so), but we should be able to do it smartly - if that includes some public popular people and public organizations and for example email was made public on the internet by organization itself we should be able to treat such data as not personal.

And all credentials (tokens, passwords and so on), which are clear from context.

The most important feature for this system is reliability so it must use all algorithms from competitors, or reimplement a more advanced algorithms here, so we bet exactly all open-source competitors in the field, and provide best possible sanitation for sensitive data on the market.

For closed source competitors we should use their docs and examples to support all their features as well.

We may also include tools to carefully redact / edit history of GitHub, to make sure sensitive data was removed from the history.

We should support as much natural languages as possible, and work with all their specifics. And as much popular services as possible where the format of credential tokens is known.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
acceptance: closed upstream; independent regression audit required
